content.text: Issue read. Codebase mapped. Three constraints matter before I plan:

questions.question: Terminal panes are Metal-backed and hidden panes stop rendering, so real bitmap screenshots of inactive panes are impossible without screen-recording permission. What should the rail cards show?

options.label: Live text preview (Recommended)
options.description: Terminal panes: render their current screen text (existing `readCommandRegion` ghostty API) into a small monospaced card in theme colours — works for occluded panes, no new frameworks/permissions. Diff/file/changeset panes are pure SwiftUI so `ImageRenderer` gives a true miniature.

options.label: Icon + label only
options.description: Like the real cmd+tab, which shows app ICONS not screenshots. Per-kind glyph (terminal/plusminus/doc/clock) + title + badges. Cheapest, ships fastest, zero capture risk.

options.label: Real screenshots
options.description: ScreenCaptureKit window capture cropped to the pane frame, cached while the pane is visible. True pixels, but a new framework, a screen-recording permission prompt, stale caches for never-shown panes, and nothing at all for a pane hidden since launch.

questions.question: macOS cmd+tab is MRU-ordered (quick tap flips between the two most-recent). The app's existing ⌥⌘←/→ cycling is positional. Which for the switcher?

options.label: MRU (Recommended)
options.description: True cmd+tab feel: rail ordered most-recently-used first, quick tap = back to the previous workroom/pane. Needs a new per-window recency list (none exists today; `NavigationHistory` is a back/forward stack, not MRU).

options.label: Positional
options.description: Rail mirrors the on-screen order (`displayedWorkroomTargets()` / `displayedTabIDs`), quick tap = next to the right. Reuses existing `cycleWorkroomTab`/`cycleTerminalTab` verbatim, and "nav follows the eye" matches the rest of the app — but is not cmd+tab behaviour.

questions.question: Where should the rail be drawn?

options.label: In-window overlay (Recommended)
options.description: Centred in the window content, reusing the `DialogOverlay` backdrop/card recipe and its titlebar-accessory dim trick. Per-window (AppStore is per-window), no window-level fights, unit- and UI-testable.

options.label: Floating screen-centred panel
options.description: Borderless non-activating NSPanel above everything, screen-centred like the real switcher. New window type (no NSPanel exists in the app), needs WindowRegistry cycle exclusion + theme wiring.

questions.question: ⌥Tab scope for workrooms — the app supports multiple windows, and each window owns its own AppStore/selection.

options.label: Current window only (Recommended)
options.description: Rail lists the open workrooms of the frontmost window; ⌘` stays the window switcher. Clean separation, no cross-window state.

options.label: All windows
options.description: Rail lists open workrooms across every window; committing may raise another window. Overlaps ⌘` and needs app-global switcher state.

# Issue #132 — Terminal/Workroom quick switcher (⌥Tab / ⌃Tab)

## Context

Workroom has positional navigation only: ⌥⌘←/→ steps terminal tabs, ⇧⌥⌘←/→ steps workroom tabs,
⌘1–9 / ⌥⌘1–9 jump by index, ⌘` cycles windows. There is no way to flip back to *what you were just
looking at*, and no way to see what's open without reading the tab bars.

Issue #132 asks for the macOS ⌘Tab experience, twice:
- **⌥Tab** — switch open **workrooms**, across **all** app windows.
- **⌃Tab** — switch the current workroom's open **detail panes** (terminals, diffs, files, changesets).

Behaviour per the issue: quick tap switches immediately; press-and-hold the trigger modifier shows a
screen-centred horizontal rail of **screenshot thumbnails** with labels; ←/→ and Tab/⇧Tab move along
the rail; mouse hover and click work; each card shows a notification count badge.

Decisions taken with the user: **real screenshots** (not text/glyph previews), **MRU ordering** (true
⌘Tab feel — a quick tap flips to the previous item), a **floating panel** so the rail can span
windows, and **all-windows scope** for ⌥Tab.

Outcome: two-key muscle memory for the two things you actually switch between all day, with a visual
rail that makes "what's open" answerable at a glance.

---

## Architecture

Three independent layers. Each is buildable and verifiable on its own; the rail reads snapshots
through an optional accessor so capture can land late (or degrade) without touching the UI.

### A. Session core (pure, headless)

`Core/QuickSwitcherReducer.swift` — state machine in the shape of `EdgeRevealReducer`
(`Views/EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:30`, tested by `WorkroomAppTests/EdgeRevealReducerTests.swift`):

```swift
enum QuickSwitcherKey { case workrooms(reverse: Bool), panes(reverse: Bool)
  nonisolated static func classify(keyCode: UInt16, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) -> QuickSwitcherKey? }

struct QuickSwitcherReducer {
  enum Kind { case workrooms, panes }
  enum Phase { case idle, pending, revealed }          // pending = live, rail not yet shown
  enum Event { case open(kind: Kind, count: Int, reverse: Bool), step(reverse: Bool), point(index: Int),
               revealTimerFired, commit(index: Int?), modifierReleased, cancel(Cancel), itemsChanged(count: Int) }
  enum Effect { case none, armReveal, reveal, moveCursor(Int), end(commit: Int?) }
  mutating func handle(_ event: Event) -> Effect
}
```

Rules (each a test):
- `.open` with `count <= 1` → stays idle, no-op (key still swallowed).
- `.open` → `cursor = reverse ? count-1 : 1`, phase `.pending`, `.armReveal` (reveal delay ~180 ms,
  injectable `Duration`, matching `EdgeRevealSidebar`'s 180 ms).
- `.step` while `.pending` → reveal immediately (⌘Tab⌘Tab behaviour) **and** move cursor.
- Commit happens **only** on modifier release / click / Return — never per step. That is what makes a
  quick tap flash-free and avoids raising windows or writing history on every step.
- **Every event while `.idle` is a no-op** — load-bearing: after a click commit the user still
  releases the modifier, and that must not double-commit.
- `.itemsChanged(0)` → end without commit; `> 0` → clamp cursor.

`Core/SwitcherRecency.swift` — MRU:

```swift
struct RecencyList<ID: Hashable> {                 // pure value type
  mutating func touch(_ id: ID); mutating func forget(_ id: ID); mutating func retain(_ live: Set<ID>)
  func ordered<T>(_ items: [T], id: (T) -> ID) -> [T]   // MRU first, never-touched appended positionally
}
struct WorkroomSlotID: Hashable { let store: ObjectIdentifier; let sid: SidebarID }
@MainActor final class SwitcherRecency { static let shared = SwitcherRecency() /* workrooms, panes */ }
```

Workroom identity is **(store, SidebarID)**, not SidebarID alone: `TerminalSessions` is per-window
(`AppStore.swift:599`), so the same workroom open in two windows is two switchable things. Use
`ObjectIdentifier(store)`, **not** `AppStore.windowNumber` — window numbers are reclaimed
(`WindowRegistry.swift:81`) and would alias a dead window's recency onto a new one. Panes key on
`TerminalTab.ID` (a UUID, already app-unique).

Recording hooks (three one-liners, all on existing single write-points):
- `AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet` (`AppStore.swift:157`) → `recordWorkroom(store:sid:)`
- `WindowRegistry`'s existing `didBecomeKeyNotification` observer (`WindowRegistry.swift:48`) →
  `recordWorkroom` — **required**, else ⌘` to another window leaves MRU[0] on the window you left
- `AppStore`'s `terminals.onFocusChange` (`AppStore.swift:828`) → `recordPane(tabID)`; prune via
  `onTabsRemoved` (`:843`) → `forgetPanes(ids)`

Rail order is computed once at session open and frozen; the commit re-orders MRU as a *consequence*
(via the hooks above), so the next tap correctly flips back.

`Core/QuickSwitcherController.swift` — the only impure piece: owns the reducer, the reveal timer, the
flagsChanged monitor, the watchdog, item collection/validation, the panel, and the commit.

### B. Key plumbing

**Two monitors.** Extend the existing `.keyDown` monitor (`WorkroomApp.swift:206`, capture `[weak self]`):

1. **First statement of the handler**, before the ⌘W branches — while a session is live the switcher
   is a modal capture like the OS HUD: Tab/⇧Tab and keyCode 123/124 step, 53 cancels, 36/76 commit,
   anything else cancels; **all** swallowed. Must be first so ⌘1–9 / ⌘W / ⌘` can't fire under a rail.
2. **Open branch immediately after the ⌘` branch** (`:236-244`) — same shape (app-global, swallowed
   behind a modal). Gate on `Self.hasModalPicker(window)` and `Self.shortcutStore(for: window)`, the
   existing injectable-registry seams (`:175`, `:185`), so ⌥Tab in Settings/About is a quiet no-op.
   Always `return nil`.

The flagsChanged monitor is **installed by the controller at session open and removed at end** — do
not widen the existing mask, or every modifier tap runs the 140-line cascade. It must always
`return event`: `GhosttySurfaceView.flagsChanged` (`:927`) forwards modifier press/release to
libghostty, and swallowing the release would leave libghostty thinking the modifier is still held.
No `.keyUp` needed (Tab autorepeat already arrives as `.keyDown`).

A local monitor returning `nil` runs inside `NSApp.sendEvent` before dispatch, so it beats both the
main menu and a focused Ghostty surface. Still add reservation as defence in depth, in
`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`:

- `isAppShortcut`: a keyCode-48 branch **before** the `charactersIgnoringModifiers` guard (~:994) —
  reserved for `.option`, `[.option,.shift]`, `.control`, `[.control,.shift]`; never bare Tab, never
  any ⌘ combo.
- `keyDown`: hoist `if isAppShortcut(event) { return }` to the top (~:833). Today the classifier is
  only consulted on the ⌘ path (`:865`) and in `performKeyEquivalent` (`:949`) — ⌃Tab takes the
  control-only branch at `:843` and ⌥Tab the IME path at `:876`, so without this the reservation is
  dead code for non-⌘ keys. Behaviour-preserving now (every non-⌘ combo currently classifies false).

### C. Screenshots

Capture **one window, crop N regions** — one round trip, one consistent frame, one epoch check.

Own-process capture, verified in the SDK header
(`ScreenCaptureKit.framework/Headers/SCShareableContent.h:151`): `SCShareableContent.currentProcess`
(macOS 14.4+, our floor is 15.0) returns content "available to capture by current process **without
user consent via TCC**". **Spike this first** (30 min: revoke Screen Recording for
`com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, capture our own window). If it holds there is no permission
story at all.

```swift
let content = try await SCShareableContent.currentProcess
let scWindow = content.windows.first { $0.windowID == CGWindowID(nsWindow.windowNumber) }
let filter = SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow: scWindow)   // ignores overlapping windows
// config: 1:1 pointPixelScale, showsCursor = false,
//         ignoreShadowsSingleWindow / ignoreGlobalClipSingleWindow = true, captureResolution = .best
let image = try await SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: filter, configuration: config)
```

`desktopIndependentWindow` captures a window that is behind others or not frontmost, and excludes
overlapping windows — so the rail panel can never contaminate a shot, **provided the panel is not
added as a child window** (`includeChildWindows` defaults to true). Gate on
`nsWindow.isVisible && !nsWindow.isMiniaturized`; on failure **keep the existing cache entry**, never
overwrite with blank.

Crop math, pure and testable — do it with CoreGraphics, not `SCStreamConfiguration.sourceRect`:

```swift
enum SnapshotGeometry {
  static func cropRect(regionOnScreen: CGRect, windowOnScreen: CGRect, imagePixelSize: CGSize) -> CGRect?
  static func thumbnailPixelSize(source: CGSize, maxPointWidth: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat) -> CGSize
}
```

Both rects live in the same y-up screen space (`view.convert(bounds, to: nil)` →
`window.convertToScreen`), so the global flip cancels: no `NSScreen` lookup, no primary-display
height, no multi-display case. Derive scale from `image.width / windowOnScreen.width` rather than
`backingScaleFactor`. Downscale into a card-sized bitmap and drop the full-window shot immediately
(a 1600×1000@2× shot is ~25 MB; a 320×200@2× thumb ~1 MB).

Hidden panes are occluded — `ghostty_surface_set_occlusion` via
`TerminalSessions.reconcileOcclusion` (`:929`) → nothing renders → **they can only be captured while
visible, then cached**:

```swift
enum SnapshotKey: Hashable { case pane(TerminalTab.ID), workroom(SidebarID, window: Int) }
struct Snapshot { let image: CGImage; let capturedAt: Date; let themeGeneration: Int }

@MainActor @Observable final class SnapshotService {           // .shared, like ThemeService
  init(capturer: SnapshotCapturing = ScreenCaptureKitCapturer(), clock: @escaping () -> Date = Date.init)
  func snapshot(for key: SnapshotKey) -> Snapshot?             // rail read; never captures, never awaits
  func noteContentChanged(window: Int)                         // debounced 0.75s, per-window floor 2s
  func noteVisibilityChanged()                                 // bumps epoch, schedules settle capture
  func captureVisibleRegions(reason: CaptureReason) async      // switcher-open: immediate, no rate limit
  func purge(_ keys: [SnapshotKey]); func purgeWindow(_ number: Int)
}
protocol SnapshotCapturing: Sendable { func captureWindow(number: Int) async throws -> CapturedWindow }
```

**Epoch guard** (same idea as `ThemeService.generation`): snapshot epoch + window frame + every
planned rect synchronously at request time; on resume, if the epoch or the window frame changed,
discard the whole shot. A pane that hid mid-capture bumps the epoch → worst case is a stale card,
never a mislabeled one. This is what makes the switch-time async race a non-issue.

Triggers — **no always-on timer**: pane/workroom became visible (`reconcileOcclusion`,
`selectedTargetID.didSet`); activity settled (existing `onTitleChange` / `onCwdChange` /
`onCommandFinished` / `onProgressReport` callbacks in `TerminalSessions`); switcher opened (fires
*before* the panel is ordered in); theme changed (bumps `themeGeneration`, older entries read stale).
Honest limit: libghostty exposes no damage/frame signal, so a shell typing without OSC output won't
refresh between those events — the switcher-open capture covers everything perceivable. The
escalation is a damage callback in the pinned fork, not a polling timer.

Cache: LRU with `maxEntries = 32` and `maxBytes = 24 MB`, injected clock, plus a
`DispatchSource.makeMemoryPressureSource` handler. Purge on `onTabsRemoved`, on workroom deletion,
and — **mandatory** — on `WindowRegistry.unregister` → `purgeWindow(store.windowNumber)`, because
window numbers are reclaimed and a stale entry would surface in a new window's cards.

Rect discovery — ask the mounted AppKit views, don't re-derive `PaneTreeLayout.plan`:

```swift
struct SnapshotRectReporter: NSViewRepresentable { let key: SnapshotKey }   // zero-drawing, bumps epoch
@MainActor final class SnapshotRegistry { static let shared: … ; var epoch: Int
  func screenRect(for key: SnapshotKey) -> (rect: CGRect, window: Int)?; var visibleKeys: [(SnapshotKey, Int)] }
```

Exactly two `.background { }` mount points, both on always-mounted views (no `_ConditionalContent`
branch flips): `PaneLeafView` (`Views/PaneTreeView.swift:383`) covers all four `TabContent` kinds
uniformly, and `WorkroomPaneLeaf` (`Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:164`) covers workrooms — solo and
split both, since `RootView.workroomSplitBody` (`:649`) always renders through `WorkroomSplitView`.

Fallback card (must exist regardless, and is what ships if the spike fails): per-`TabContent` SF
Symbol + title + badge, reusing the `TerminalTabStrip` glyph vocabulary (`plusminus` / `doc` /
`clock` / `terminal`). If capture proves unworkable, the strong plan B is a text preview from
`GhosttySurfaceView.readCommandRegion` (`:777`) + `TerminalCapture.tidy` — permission-free and it
works for hidden panes.

If the spike shows TCC *is* required: `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` for status (never prompt at
launch), `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` only from an explicit in-rail "Turn on window previews"
affordance, deep link to `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture`,
re-preflight on `didBecomeActive`, and a `Defaults[.railPreviews]` opt-out. Screen Recording needs no
entitlement and no Info.plist key; keep `CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS: NO` (`project.yml:299`).
Add `- sdk: ScreenCaptureKit.framework` to `project.yml` (~:224).

### D. Panel + rail

`Core/SwitcherPanel.swift` — first `NSPanel` in the app; model on `QuickTerminalController.createWindow()`
(`:86`) and its `.themeDidChange` observer (`:118`).

```swift
final class SwitcherPanel: NSPanel {
  override var canBecomeKey: Bool { false }      // load-bearing
  override var canBecomeMain: Bool { false }
}
```

`[.nonactivatingPanel, .borderless]`, `isFloatingPanel = true`, `level = .floating`,
`collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .ignoresCycle, .transient]`,
`isOpaque = false`, `backgroundColor = .clear`, `hasShadow = false` (the card draws its own),
`isReleasedWhenClosed = false`, `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true`, `acceptsMouseMovedEvents = true`,
`animationBehavior = .none`, a11y id `switcher.panel`.

`canBecomeKey == false` is what makes the design work: the workroom window stays `NSApp.keyWindow`,
so the monitor's `event.window ?? NSApp.keyWindow` (`:234`) keeps resolving the real store and keys

`canBecomeKey`, and `.ignoresCycle` covers the system. Drop `private` from `isCycleableWindow` so a
test can assert it.

click is eaten) plus `acceptsMouseMovedEvents`; `.onHover` works via `NSTrackingArea`.

`min(intrinsic, visibleFrame.width - 80)` with horizontal scroll on overflow.

The panel must never touch an `AppStore` (there isn't one) — the controller feeds it value-type
snapshots via `SwitcherRailModel` (`items: [SwitcherCard]`, `cursor`, `themeVersion`, `onHover`,
`onCommit`).

# Issue #132 — Terminal/Workroom quick switcher (⌥Tab / ⌃Tab)

## Context

Workroom has positional navigation only: ⌥⌘←/→ steps terminal tabs, ⇧⌥⌘←/→ steps workroom tabs,
⌘1–9 / ⌥⌘1–9 jump by index, ⌘` cycles windows. There is no way to flip back to *what you were just
looking at*, and no way to see what's open without reading the tab bars.

Issue #132 asks for the macOS ⌘Tab experience, twice:
- **⌥Tab** — switch open **workrooms**, across **all** app windows.
- **⌃Tab** — switch the current workroom's open **detail panes** (terminals, diffs, files, changesets).

Behaviour per the issue: quick tap switches immediately; press-and-hold the trigger modifier shows a
screen-centred horizontal rail of **screenshot thumbnails** with labels; ←/→ and Tab/⇧Tab move along
the rail; mouse hover and click work; each card shows a notification count badge.

Decisions taken with the user: **real screenshots** (not text/glyph previews), **MRU ordering** (true
⌘Tab feel — a quick tap flips to the previous item), a **floating panel** so the rail can span
windows, and **all-windows scope** for ⌥Tab.

Outcome: two-key muscle memory for the two things you actually switch between all day, with a visual
rail that makes "what's open" answerable at a glance.

---

## Architecture

Three independent layers. Each is buildable and verifiable on its own; the rail reads snapshots
through an optional accessor so capture can land late (or degrade) without touching the UI.

### A. Session core (pure, headless)

`Core/QuickSwitcherReducer.swift` — state machine in the shape of `EdgeRevealReducer`
(`Views/EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:30`, tested by `WorkroomAppTests/EdgeRevealReducerTests.swift`):

```swift
enum QuickSwitcherKey { case workrooms(reverse: Bool), panes(reverse: Bool)
  nonisolated static func classify(keyCode: UInt16, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) -> QuickSwitcherKey? }

struct QuickSwitcherReducer {
  enum Kind { case workrooms, panes }
  enum Phase { case idle, pending, revealed }          // pending = live, rail not yet shown
  enum Event { case open(kind: Kind, count: Int, reverse: Bool), step(reverse: Bool), point(index: Int),
               revealTimerFired, commit(index: Int?), modifierReleased, cancel(Cancel), itemsChanged(count: Int) }
  enum Effect { case none, armReveal, reveal, moveCursor(Int), end(commit: Int?) }
  mutating func handle(_ event: Event) -> Effect
}
```

Rules (each a test):
- `.open` with `count <= 1` → stays idle, no-op (key still swallowed).
- `.open` → `cursor = reverse ? count-1 : 1`, phase `.pending`, `.armReveal` (reveal delay ~180 ms,
  injectable `Duration`, matching `EdgeRevealSidebar`'s 180 ms).
- `.step` while `.pending` → reveal immediately (⌘Tab⌘Tab behaviour) **and** move cursor.
- Commit happens **only** on modifier release / click / Return — never per step. That is what makes a
  quick tap flash-free and avoids raising windows or writing history on every step.
- **Every event while `.idle` is a no-op** — load-bearing: after a click commit the user still
  releases the modifier, and that must not double-commit.
- `.itemsChanged(0)` → end without commit; `> 0` → clamp cursor.

`Core/SwitcherRecency.swift` — MRU:

```swift
struct RecencyList<ID: Hashable> {                 // pure value type
  mutating func touch(_ id: ID); mutating func forget(_ id: ID); mutating func retain(_ live: Set<ID>)
  func ordered<T>(_ items: [T], id: (T) -> ID) -> [T]   // MRU first, never-touched appended positionally
}
struct WorkroomSlotID: Hashable { let store: ObjectIdentifier; let sid: SidebarID }
@MainActor final class SwitcherRecency { static let shared = SwitcherRecency() /* workrooms, panes */ }
```

Workroom identity is **(store, SidebarID)**, not SidebarID alone: `TerminalSessions` is per-window
(`AppStore.swift:599`), so the same workroom open in two windows is two switchable things. Use
`ObjectIdentifier(store)`, **not** `AppStore.windowNumber` — window numbers are reclaimed
(`WindowRegistry.swift:81`) and would alias a dead window's recency onto a new one. Panes key on
`TerminalTab.ID` (a UUID, already app-unique).

Recording hooks (three one-liners, all on existing single write-points):
- `AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet` (`AppStore.swift:157`) → `recordWorkroom(store:sid:)`
- `WindowRegistry`'s existing `didBecomeKeyNotification` observer (`WindowRegistry.swift:48`) →
  `recordWorkroom` — **required**, else ⌘` to another window leaves MRU[0] on the window you left
- `AppStore`'s `terminals.onFocusChange` (`AppStore.swift:828`) → `recordPane(tabID)`; prune via
  `onTabsRemoved` (`:843`) → `forgetPanes(ids)`

Rail order is computed once at session open and frozen; the commit re-orders MRU as a *consequence*
(via the hooks above), so the next tap correctly flips back.

`Core/QuickSwitcherController.swift` — the only impure piece: owns the reducer, the reveal timer, the
flagsChanged monitor, the watchdog, item collection/validation, the panel, and the commit.

### B. Key plumbing

**Two monitors.** Extend the existing `.keyDown` monitor (`WorkroomApp.swift:206`, capture `[weak self]`):

1. **First statement of the handler**, before the ⌘W branches — while a session is live the switcher
   is a modal capture like the OS HUD: Tab/⇧Tab and keyCode 123/124 step, 53 cancels, 36/76 commit,
   anything else cancels; **all** swallowed. Must be first so ⌘1–9 / ⌘W / ⌘` can't fire under a rail.
2. **Open branch immediately after the ⌘` branch** (`:236-244`) — same shape (app-global, swallowed

   existing injectable-registry seams (`:175`, `:185`), so ⌥Tab in Settings/About is a quiet no-op.
   Always `return nil`.

The flagsChanged monitor is **installed by the controller at session open and removed at end** — do
not widen the existing mask, or every modifier tap runs the 140-line cascade. It must always
`return event`: `GhosttySurfaceView.flagsChanged` (`:927`) forwards modifier press/release to
libghostty, and swallowing the release would leave libghostty thinking the modifier is still held.
No `.keyUp` needed (Tab autorepeat already arrives as `.keyDown`).

A local monitor returning `nil` runs inside `NSApp.sendEvent` before dispatch, so it beats both the
main menu and a focused Ghostty surface. Still add reservation as defence in depth, in

  reserved for `.option`, `[.option,.shift]`, `.control`, `[.control,.shift]`; never bare Tab, never
  any ⌘ combo.
- `keyDown`: hoist `if isAppShortcut(event) { return }` to the top (~:833). Today the classifier is
  only consulted on the ⌘ path (`:865`) and in `performKeyEquivalent` (`:949`) — ⌃Tab takes the
  control-only branch at `:843` and ⌥Tab the IME path at `:876`, so without this the reservation is
  dead code for non-⌘ keys. Behaviour-preserving now (every non-⌘ combo currently classifies false).

### C. Screenshots

Capture **one window, crop N regions** — one round trip, one consistent frame, one epoch check.

Own-process capture, verified in the SDK header
(`ScreenCaptureKit.framework/Headers/SCShareableContent.h:151`): `SCShareableContent.currentProcess`
(macOS 14.4+, our floor is 15.0) returns content "available to capture by current process **without
user consent via TCC**". **Spike this first** (30 min: revoke Screen Recording for
`com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, capture our own window). If it holds there is no permission
story at all.

```swift
let content = try await SCShareableContent.currentProcess
let scWindow = content.windows.first { $0.windowID == CGWindowID(nsWindow.windowNumber) }
let filter = SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow: scWindow)   // ignores overlapping windows
// config: 1:1 pointPixelScale, showsCursor = false,
//         ignoreShadowsSingleWindow / ignoreGlobalClipSingleWindow = true, captureResolution = .best
let image = try await SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: filter, configuration: config)
```

`desktopIndependentWindow` captures a window that is behind others or not frontmost, and excludes
overlapping windows — so the rail panel can never contaminate a shot, **provided the panel is not
added as a child window** (`includeChildWindows` defaults to true). Gate on
`nsWindow.isVisible && !nsWindow.isMiniaturized`; on failure **keep the existing cache entry**, never
overwrite with blank.

Crop math, pure and testable — do it with CoreGraphics, not `SCStreamConfiguration.sourceRect`:

```swift
enum SnapshotGeometry {
  static func cropRect(regionOnScreen: CGRect, windowOnScreen: CGRect, imagePixelSize: CGSize) -> CGRect?
  static func thumbnailPixelSize(source: CGSize, maxPointWidth: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat) -> CGSize
}
```

Both rects live in the same y-up screen space (`view.convert(bounds, to: nil)` →
`window.convertToScreen`), so the global flip cancels: no `NSScreen` lookup, no primary-display
height, no multi-display case. Derive scale from `image.width / windowOnScreen.width` rather than
`backingScaleFactor`. Downscale into a card-sized bitmap and drop the full-window shot immediately
(a 1600×1000@2× shot is ~25 MB; a 320×200@2× thumb ~1 MB).

Hidden panes are occluded — `ghostty_surface_set_occlusion` via
`TerminalSessions.reconcileOcclusion` (`:929`) → nothing renders → **they can only be captured while
visible, then cached**:

```swift
  func snapshot(for key: SnapshotKey) -> Snapshot?             // rail read; never captures, never awaits
  func noteContentChanged(window: Int)                         // debounced 0.75s, per-window floor 2s
```

**Epoch guard** (same idea as `ThemeService.generation`): snapshot epoch + window frame + every
planned rect synchronously at request time; on resume, if the epoch or the window frame changed,
discard the whole shot. A pane that hid mid-capture bumps the epoch → worst case is a stale card,
never a mislabeled one. This is what makes the switch-time async race a non-issue.

Triggers — **no always-on timer**: pane/workroom became visible (`reconcileOcclusion`,
`selectedTargetID.didSet`); activity settled (existing `onTitleChange` / `onCwdChange` /
`onCommandFinished` / `onProgressReport` callbacks in `TerminalSessions`); switcher opened (fires
*before* the panel is ordered in); theme changed (bumps `themeGeneration`, older entries read stale).
Honest limit: libghostty exposes no damage/frame signal, so a shell typing without OSC output won't
refresh between those events — the switcher-open capture covers everything perceivable. The
escalation is a damage callback in the pinned fork, not a polling timer.

Cache: LRU with `maxEntries = 32` and `maxBytes = 24 MB`, injected clock, plus a
`DispatchSource.makeMemoryPressureSource` handler. Purge on `onTabsRemoved`, on workroom deletion,
and — **mandatory** — on `WindowRegistry.unregister` → `purgeWindow(store.windowNumber)`, because
window numbers are reclaimed and a stale entry would surface in a new window's cards.

Rect discovery — ask the mounted AppKit views, don't re-derive `PaneTreeLayout.plan`:

works for hidden panes.

0. **Spike** `SCShareableContent.currentProcess` + `SCScreenshotManager` with Screen Recording revoked.
1. Pure core: reducer, `RecencyList`, classifier, `SnapshotGeometry`/`SnapshotPolicy`/`SnapshotCache` + tests. No behaviour change.
2. Recency hooks in `AppStore` / `WindowRegistry` (verified with two stores, `MultiWindowTests` pattern).
3. **Tap-only, no panel**: monitor branches, `isAppShortcut` + `keyDown` hoist, commit path. ⌥Tab/⌃Tab work end-to-end and no longer reach TUIs — independently shippable, and most of the value.
4. Hold detection: flagsChanged monitor, reveal timer, watchdog, `didResignActive` / `willClose` observers. **Do not ship step 5 before this.**
5. Panel + rail with fallback (glyph) cards.
6. `SnapshotRegistry` + reporter (verify rects with a temporary debug overlay), then `SnapshotService` + `ScreenCaptureKitCapturer` + triggers; swap cards to real thumbnails.


Manual (`make app-run`, two windows, ≥3 workrooms, ≥3 panes, at least one busy agent pane):
- Quick ⌥Tab tap flips to the previous workroom with **no rail flash**; tapping again flips back.
- Hold ⌥ → rail appears centred; ⇧⌥Tab and ←/→ walk it; release commits; Escape cancels with no change.
- ⌥Tab reaches a workroom in the **other** window: that window raises and selects.
- ⌃Tab does the same for panes within the current workroom; committed pane takes keyboard focus.
- Both work with a **focused TUI** (Claude/Codex in a pane) — the terminal must not see the keys.
  Model on `WorkroomAppUITests/ViewMenuShortcutsUITests.swift`'s `focusATerminal(_:)`.
- Thumbnails: correct pane content, correct after a theme switch, after dragging a window between
  Retina and non-Retina displays, and for a workroom not selected since launch (fallback card).
- Notification badge counts match the sidebar/tab-bar badges.
- No stuck rail: ⌥Tab then ⌘Tab away; ⌥Tab then click another app; ⌥Tab then close the window.
- Hover/click with a **real mouse** — synthetic accessibility clicks do not reproduce hit-testing on
  a non-key panel.
- ⌘` still cycles windows and never lands on the panel.

## Risks / trade-offs

- **Reserving ⌃Tab takes `<C-Tab>` away from TUIs** (Neovim buffer cycling, some pickers) — the
  explicit ask, but call it out in the PR; keep a `Defaults` key for the pane-switcher modifier in
  reserve. ⌥Tab is safe (unused by macOS and by common TUIs).
- **Own-process capture may still hit TCC** — step 0 decides; the fallback ladder (glyph card →
  `readCommandRegion` text preview) means the feature degrades, never breaks.
- **Stuck rail** from a lost modifier release (menu tracking and other modal run loops don't feed
  local monitors). Mitigated by `didResignActive` + a 100 ms `NSEvent.modifierFlags` watchdog +
  Escape + a 10 s ceiling. All four.
- **Hidden-pane thumbnails are inherently frozen** (occlusion) — cache-while-visible; don't promise
  "live" in UI copy.
- **Monitor branch ordering** is load-bearing: live-session capture first, open branch after ⌘`.
- `selectedTargetID.didSet` is already heavy — the recency write must stay O(1) and touch no stores.

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)


## Artifacts Sync (skill start)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users
# upgrading mid-stream before the migration script runs.
if [ -f "$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt" ]; then
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt"
else
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt"
fi
_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync"
_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# /sync-gbrain context-load: teach the agent to use gbrain when it's available.
# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
  if [ -f "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" ]; then
    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))
    [ "$_BRAIN_AGE" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0
  fi
  if [ "$_BRAIN_DO_PULL" = "1" ]; then
    ( cd "$_GSTACK_HOME" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true
    echo "$_BRAIN_NOW" > "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE"
  fi
  "$_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN" --once 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ "$_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE" = "remote-http" ]; then
```

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.

## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
* Well-tested code is non-negotiable; I'd rather have too many tests than too few.
* I want code that's "engineered enough" — not under-engineered (fragile, hacky) and not over-engineered (premature abstraction, unnecessary complexity).
* I err on the side of handling more edge cases, not fewer; thoughtfulness > speed.
* Bias toward explicit over clever.
* Right-sized diff: favor the smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change ... but don't compress a necessary rewrite into a minimal patch. If the existing foundation is broken, say "scrap it and do this instead."

## Cognitive Patterns — How Great Eng Managers Think

These are not additional checklist items. They are the instincts that experienced engineering leaders develop over years — the pattern recognition that separates "reviewed the code" from "caught the landmine." Apply them throughout your review.

1. **State diagnosis** — Teams exist in four states: falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. Each demands a different intervention (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle).
2. **Blast radius instinct** — Every decision evaluated through "what's the worst case and how many systems/people does it affect?"
3. **Boring by default** — "Every company gets about three innovation tokens." Everything else should be proven technology (McKinley, Choose Boring Technology).
4. **Incremental over revolutionary** — Strangler fig, not big bang. Canary, not global rollout. Refactor, not rewrite (Fowler).
5. **Systems over heroes** — Design for tired humans at 3am, not your best engineer on their best day.
6. **Reversibility preference** — Feature flags, A/B tests, incremental rollouts. Make the cost of being wrong low.
7. **Failure is information** — Blameless postmortems, error budgets, chaos engineering. Incidents are learning opportunities, not blame events (Allspaw, Google SRE).
8. **Org structure IS architecture** — Conway's Law in practice. Design both intentionally (Skelton/Pais, Team Topologies).
9. **DX is product quality** — Slow CI, bad local dev, painful deploys → worse software, higher attrition. Developer experience is a leading indicator.
10. **Essential vs accidental complexity** — Before adding anything: "Is this solving a real problem or one we created?" (Brooks, No Silver Bullet).
11. **Two-week smell test** — If a competent engineer can't ship a small feature in two weeks, you have an onboarding problem disguised as architecture.
12. **Glue work awareness** — Recognize invisible coordination work. Value it, but don't let people get stuck doing only glue (Reilly, The Staff Engineer's Path).
13. **Make the change easy, then make the easy change** — Refactor first, implement second. Never structural + behavioral changes simultaneously (Beck).
14. **Own your code in production** — No wall between dev and ops. "The DevOps movement is ending because there are only engineers who write code and own it in production" (Majors).
15. **Error budgets over uptime targets** — SLO of 99.9% = 0.1% downtime *budget to spend on shipping*. Reliability is resource allocation (Google SRE).

When evaluating architecture, think "boring by default." When reviewing tests, think "systems over heroes." When assessing complexity, ask Brooks's question. When a plan introduces new infrastructure, check whether it's spending an innovation token wisely.

## Operationals
- [git-diff-rejects-pathspec-from-file] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-02)
  `git diff` and `git status` do NOT accept --pathspec-from-file (measured: `error: invalid option: --pathspec-from-file=-`), even though `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git reset`, `git rm` and `git stash` all do. So a path-scoped diff cannot be fed paths on stdin and would need argv (E2BIG risk on large selections). Better technique for asking `which of these paths have staged content that a --only commit would discard`: run `git status --porcelain -z` UNFILTERED and filter in memory on the two status columns. X is HEAD->index, Y is index->worktree, so `MM` = partly staged and AT RISK, `M ` = staged and identical to disk (safe), ` M` = never staged (safe), `??` = untracked (safe). -z is required because a filename can contain a newline and git C-quotes non-ASCII names otherwise; a rename/copy entry (X in R,C) spends a SECOND NUL field on its old path, so a parser must consume it or the whole walk desyncs.
- [git-pathspec-glob-magic-after-double-dash] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-01)
  A git pathspec after `--` still honours GLOB MAGIC: `git add -- a[b].txt` also stages ab.txt, and a file literally named * stages the whole tree. `--` ends OPTION parsing, not MAGIC parsing. Measured on throwaway repos. Fix: --pathspec-from-file=- with --pathspec-file-nul (paths taken literally, also removes argv E2BIG), or a :(literal) prefix per path. Related: `git commit -- <path>` implies --only and DISCARDS staged content for that path (data loss after git add -p), and --only alone cannot commit an untracked file, so a preceding `git add` is mandatory. jj is worse: paths are a fileset EXPRESSION language, a space hard-fails to parse, and a fileset matching nothing still creates an empty commit and exits 0.

- [wr-vcs-core-reads-no-user-config] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-01)
  wr-vcs-core builds UserSettings from StackedConfig::with_defaults() at jj_backend.rs:84,593,987, so jj-lib sees empty user.name/user.email and signing.backend=none. That's a lot of small parts for a feature whose *keyboard* half (quick tap flips workrooms/panes by recency) is only about six files and delivers most of the daily value on its own. Two independent reductions are available: ship the keyboard half first, and collapse the snapshot subsystem into fewer files with the speculative extras (memory-pressure eviction, per-window rate limiter) deferred until measured.

## Operationals
- [git-diff-rejects-pathspec-from-file] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-02)
  `git diff` and `git status` do NOT accept --pathspec-from-file (measured: `error: invalid option: --pathspec-from-file=-`), even though `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git reset`, `git rm` and `git stash` all do. So a path-scoped diff cannot be fed paths on stdin and would need argv (E2BIG risk on large selections). Better technique for asking `which of these paths have staged content that a --only commit would discard`: run `git status --porcelain -z` UNFILTERED and filter in memory on the two status columns. X is HEAD->index, Y is index->worktree, so `MM` = partly staged and AT RISK, `M ` = staged and identical to disk (safe), ` M` = never staged (safe), `??` = untracked (safe). -z is required because a filename can contain a newline and git C-quotes non-ASCII names otherwise; a rename/copy entry (X in R,C) spends a SECOND NUL field on its old path, so a parser must consume it or the whole walk desyncs.
- [git-pathspec-glob-magic-after-double-dash] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-01)
  A git pathspec after `--` still honours GLOB MAGIC: `git add -- a[b].txt` also stages ab.txt, and a file literally named * stages the whole tree. `--` ends OPTION parsing, not MAGIC parsing. Measured on throwaway repos. Fix: --pathspec-from-file=- with --pathspec-file-nul (paths taken literally, also removes argv E2BIG), or a :(literal) prefix per path. Related: `git commit -- <path>` implies --only and DISCARDS staged content for that path (data loss after git add -p), and --only alone cannot commit an untracked file, so a preceding `git add` is mandatory. jj is worse: paths are a fileset EXPRESSION language, a space hard-fails to parse, and a fileset matching nothing still creates an empty commit and exits 0.
- [nightly-workflow-skips-sentry-dsym-upload] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-08-04)
  macapp release.sh:110-118 uploads dSYMs only when sentry-cli is installed AND SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN/ORG/PROJECT are set, and it degrades with a plain echo. release.yml wires all four (brew :62, env :97-99) but nightly.yml does NOT (brew :141 lacks sentry-cli, build env :162-174 lacks SENTRY_*), so every nightly silently shipped unsymbolicated - why WORKROOM-2B came back with three unknown Workroom Nightly frames. Nightly also reports Sentry environment production (SentryConfig.swift:27-33) because the Nightly config is release-type. Two traps when fixing: brew install in an UNATTENDED cron must be tolerant (|| echo ::warning::) or a tap outage costs the whole nightly, and a skip-only warning cannot prove the upload happened - emit ::notice:: on success too. Also Sentry 9.19 manual-lifecycle profiling requires an explicit stopProfiler() and continuous profiles are not guaranteed to attach to app-hang events, so a launch-start-never-stop profiler is no substitute for symbols. - [statuscommandrunner-env-and-stdin-gaps] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-07-31)
  macapp StatusCommandRunner (:45-63) launches via /usr/bin/env, sets ONLY PATH plus GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, unsets GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, and NEVER assigns proc.standardInput — so the child inherits the apps stdin (a live terminal under `make app-run`) and cannot see anything from the users shell. content.text:
## Section 1 — Architecture review

**Prior learning applied: `macapp-row-observes-sessions-invalidation-storm` (confidence 9/10, from 2026-08-04)** — the plan's rail already reads value-type snapshots into `SwitcherRailModel` and holds no `AppStore`/`TerminalSessions`. Keep that hard: a rail card that observed `TerminalSessions` to compute "is cursor" would re-run at OSC frequency, which is exactly the WORKROOM-2B hang. No change needed, but it goes in the plan as an explicit invariant.

Findings:

**[P1] (confidence: 9/10) `Core/AppStore.swift:3703` + `:836` — MRU would not record on switcher commits or ⌘[ back-nav.** The commit path runs through `applyLocation`, which suppresses both recording seams for its whole body:
```swift
isNavigatingHistory = true
defer { isNavigatingHistory = false }      // AppStore.swift:3703-3704
```
and the pane hook is gated by it:
```swift
guard !self.isNavigatingHistory else { return }   // AppStore.swift:836
self.recordCurrentLocation()
```
The plan asserts "re-ordering happens as a consequence of the commit (selection change → hook #1/#3 → touch)". That is only true if the recency write sits *outside* that guard.

**[P1] (confidence: 9/10) plan §A vs §C — two different identities for "which window".** MRU keys on `ObjectIdentifier(store)`; the snapshot key uses `AppStore.windowNumber`. `windowNumber` is deliberately reclaimed:
```swift
guard store.windowNumber == 0 else { return }
let used = Set(entries.compactMap { $0.store?.windowNumber }.filter { $0 > 0 })   // :83
```
so the two identities disagree exactly when a window closes and a new one opens. Two keys for one concept, and one of them is unsafe.

**[P2] (confidence: 8/10) `WorkroomApp.swift:178` — committing into a window that has a modal up.** Suppression is gated on the *key* window (`shortcutStore` returns nil when `store.activePicker != nil`), but the all-windows rail can commit into a *different* window whose store has `activePicker` or a sheet — moving that window's selection behind its own modal.

**[P2] (confidence: 9/10) `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:844` + `WorkroomApp.swift:257` — ⌃Tab consumption policy.** The plan swallows ⌃Tab unconditionally. Today ⌃Tab reaches the TUI via the control-only branch, and the app's own convention for the workroom-cycle keys is to consume *only when the action fired* ("Consumed only when there's an Nth tab to switch to"). A single-pane workroom has nothing to switch to.

**[Note] (confidence: 6/10) `GhosttySurfaceView.applyOcclusionState` — panel/occlusion interaction.** A floating panel over a window could in principle flip `NSWindow.occlusionState` and freeze terminal rendering mid-session. The panel is small and transparent so this likely never triggers; it goes on the QA list rather than being designed around.

Starting with the first.

questions.question:
D4 — A1: MRU recording is suppressed by `isNavigatingHistory`. Where should the recency write go? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-arch-mru-hooks>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: The switcher's whole promise is "tap ⌥Tab and land on the thing you were just in". That needs a recency list, and the plan updates it from two existing hooks. Problem: both hooks sit behind a flag the app raises while it *replays* navigation — `applyLocation` sets `isNavigatingHistory = true` for its entire body (AppStore.swift:3703), and the pane hook returns early on it (`guard !self.isNavigatingHistory else { return }`, AppStore.swift:836). The switcher's own commit goes through `applyLocation`. So if the recency write is added next to `recordCurrentLocation()`, the switcher would never record where it just took you, and the next ⌥Tab tap would send you back to the same place forever — a switcher that only ever ping-pongs to one item.

Stakes if we pick wrong: the headline behaviour silently breaks in the most-used case, and it breaks in a way that looks like the ordering logic is wrong rather than the hook placement — easy to spend an hour in the wrong file.

Recommendation: A — recency is "where did the user actually end up", which is true for a switcher commit, a ⌘[ back-nav, and a sidebar click alike. History suppression exists to avoid phantom *history* entries, which is a different question.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=7/10.

Maps to your preference for explicit over clever: one unconditional write at the single selection write-point beats three call sites that each have to remember to record.

Net: record recency on every real arrival, or hand-record it at the switcher and accept that other navigation drifts the "previous" pointer.

options.label: Record unconditionally (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Place the `recordWorkroom`/`recordPane` write ABOVE the `isNavigatingHistory` guard in both `selectedTargetID.didSet` and `onFocusChange`, with a comment saying why recency and history diverge here.
✅ Every arrival updates MRU — switcher commit, ⌘[/⌘], sidebar click, ⌘1–9, notification click — so the rail order always matches lived experience.
❌ Adds one more unconditional statement to `selectedTargetID.didSet`, which is already a heavy nine-statement observer. (human: ~10min / CC: ~2min)

options.label: Gate it like history
options.description:
✅ Symmetrical with the existing `recordCurrentLocation()` call — one rule for both, nothing new to explain.
✅ Guarantees history replay can never perturb the switcher's frozen ordering mid-session.
❌ Breaks the feature: switcher commits and ⌘[ back-nav go through `applyLocation`, so MRU never advances and ⌥Tab ping-pongs to one fixed item.

options.label: Record only in the controller
options.description:
✅ Keeps `AppStore` untouched — zero new statements in the hot `didSet`, and the recency store stays entirely owned by the switcher.
✅ No risk of a history replay perturbing MRU at all.
❌ Sidebar clicks, ⌘1–9, ⌘[/⌘] and notification jumps do not update recency, so "previous" silently diverges from where you actually were — the exact drift class the app already fixed once for `lastActiveStore`.

questions.question:
D5 — A2: MRU keys on `ObjectIdentifier(store)`, snapshots key on `windowNumber` — which one identity? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-arch-window-identity>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: Both halves of the switcher need to say "this workroom, in *that* window". The plan invented two different ways to say it: recency uses the store object's address, snapshots use `AppStore.windowNumber`. Those are not interchangeable — `assignWindowNumberIfNeeded` (WindowRegistry.swift:81-86) hands out the lowest unused number, so close window 2 and open a new one and it becomes window 2 again. The recency entry for the dead window is gone; the snapshot entry is not, so a fresh window can show the previous window's thumbnails until you overwrite them. Two names for one concept is also the DRY smell you asked me to flag hard.

Stakes if we pick wrong: worst case is a rail card showing a screenshot of a workroom in a window that no longer exists — visually convincing and completely wrong, which is the one failure class the epoch guard was designed to prevent everywhere else.

Recommendation: A — one `WindowToken` type wrapping `ObjectIdentifier(store)` used by BOTH subsystems; `windowNumber` reverts to what it already is, a display string (`AppStore.swift:1068` `"Window \(windowNumber)"`).

Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=5/10.

Maps to your DRY preference plus explicit-over-clever: the identity becomes a named type instead of two incidental integers/pointers.

Net: one unambiguous identity, or two that agree until a window closes.

options.label: One WindowToken for both (recommended)
options.description:

D8 — CQ1: `openExisting` already does what the plan's new `revealWorkroom` would do. Reuse or add? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-cq-1>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: The plan wanted a new one-line method on AppStore to commit a workroom switch. But `openExisting(_:)` (AppStore.swift:3775) is already that method — it activates the app and calls `applyLocation(target: sid, tab: nil, recordHistory: true)`, which selects the workroom and restores whichever tab you last had focused there. The plan's only stated reason for a new wrapper was to skip the `NSApp.activate` call, but the switcher controller was going to make that call itself when the app isn't frontmost, so there is nothing to skip.

Stakes if we pick wrong: adding a second method means two entry points that must stay in step forever. When someone later changes how a workroom switch records history or restores its tab, they will fix one and not the other — the classic pair-drift bug.

Recommendation: A — call `openExisting` and delete the new wrapper from the plan. `applyLocation` stays private, which preserves the `isNavigatingHistory` invariant it carries.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=10/10, C=9/10 — same behaviour, different amount of surface area.

**Conflict check — verified in code, plus system/third-party:**

In-app: **clean.** Tab (keyCode 48) appears in zero bindings — `rg` finds no `keyCode == 48`, no `.keyboardShortcut(.tab…)`, no `onKeyPress(.tab)`. The only keyCodes the app matches are 50 (grave, ⌘`), 123/124 (←/→) and 125/126 (⌘↑/⌘↓ scroll). So ⌥Tab, ⌃Tab and both ⇧ variants are unclaimed by menus, the monitor, and `isAppShortcut`.

Terminal side: **no user keybind can claim them.** The app loads exactly one ghostty config file — `ghostty_config_load_file(cfg, themeConfigURL)` (`Core/GhosttyApp.swift:189`) — and never `ghostty_config_load_default_files`, so `~/.config/ghostty/config` keybinds are not in play. libghostty itself ships no ⌥Tab/⌃Tab default.

macOS system:
- ⌥Tab / ⇧⌥Tab — not a system shortcut. Free.
- ⌃Tab / ⇧⌃Tab — two soft overlaps. AppKit's native window tabbing "Show Next Tab" is ⌃Tab, already dead here (`NSWindow.allowsAutomaticWindowTabbing = false`, `WorkroomApp.swift:197`). Full Keyboard Access uses ⌃Tab for "move focus to next grouping" inside dialogs/tab views — the app has no groupings to traverse, so nothing is lost.
- ⌘Tab stays the OS app switcher; we never match `.command` with keyCode 48.

The one real conflict is third-party: **AltTab.app defaults to ⌥Tab** (confidence 8/10), and rcmd/Contexts/Witch/BetterTouchTool users often bind it too. Those register a global hotkey or an event tap, which wins *before* a local monitor — so for those users ⌥Tab would never reach Workroom, and it would look like the feature is broken rather than shadowed. D9 — A5: ⌥Tab is AltTab.app's default, and a global hotkey beats our local monitor. Handle it now or later? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-arch-hotkey-conflict>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: Our shortcut is caught by `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents` (WorkroomApp.swift:206), which only sees keys the OS has already decided to deliver to us. A tool that registers ⌥Tab as a system-wide hotkey or an event tap — AltTab, Witch, Contexts, rcmd, Karabiner, BetterTouchTool — intercepts first, so Workroom never sees the keystroke. There is no API to detect that and no way to win: it is a genuine dead end for those users, not a bug we can fix in our code. The only question is whether they get an escape hatch, and when.

Stakes if we pick wrong: an AltTab user installs the release, presses ⌥Tab, sees AltTab's own window switcher, and files "the quick switcher doesn't work". We'd chase a phantom for a while before someone remembers.

Recommendation: A — ship a `Defaults` key for each switcher's modifier now (⌥ or ⌃ or ⌘⌥, say), default unchanged, exposed in Settings later if anyone asks. The classifier already has to take the modifier as data for the ⌃Tab-passthrough decision, so making it a stored preference is a small delta now and an awkward retrofit after `isAppShortcut`, the monitor branch, the tests, and the shortcuts sheet all hard-code ⌥ and ⌃.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=8/10.

Maps to your "engineered enough" line: a stored modifier is one enum and one Defaults key, not a keybinding system.

Net: a cheap escape hatch built in while the code is being written, versus finding out from an issue report and retrofitting through five files.

❌ AltTab users have no recourse at all, and adding the preference later means touching the monitor, the classifier, its tests, the shortcuts sheet, and Settings in one retrofit diff.

D10 — CQ2: the wrap step is written twice already; the reducer makes three. Extract it? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-cq-2>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: Two existing methods step an index with wraparound using the identical expression — `next = (current + (forward ? 1 : -1) + tabs.count) % tabs.count` in `cycleWorkroomTab` (AppStore.swift:1156) and again in `cycleTerminalTab` (AppStore.swift:3444). The switcher's cursor movement needs the same thing, which would be the third copy. It is one line, so this is a taste call about whether one-line duplication counts — but you asked me to flag repetition aggressively, and the switcher is the moment when "twice" becomes "a pattern".

Stakes if we pick wrong: low either way. The realistic downside of leaving it is that an off-by-one fix (or a change from wrapping to clamping) lands in two of three sites.

Recommendation: A — extract one pure `nonisolated static func wrapped(index:by:count:)`, use it in all three, and refactor the two existing callers in the same PR. Both existing sites are already covered by tests, so the refactor is verified for free — make the change easy, then make the easy change.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=7/10.

Maps to DRY plus your right-sized-diff preference: three lines deleted, one helper added, no behaviour change.

Net: one wrap rule with one test, versus three copies of a line that is easy to get subtly wrong.

options.description:

## Section 3 — Test review

Framework: XCTest via `make app-test` (`WorkroomAppTests`, 150 files, headless) + XCUITest via `make app-uitest` (`WorkroomAppUITests`, deliberately outside the main scheme). Regression coverage for the wrap-math extraction already exists in `WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomsViewTests.swift` (the only file exercising `cycleWorkroomTab`/`cycleTerminalTab`).

```
CODE PATHS                                                  USER FLOWS
[+] Core/QuickSwitcherKey (classify)                        [+] Quick tap (no rail)
  ├── [GAP] ⌥Tab / ⇧⌥Tab / ⌃Tab / ⇧⌃Tab → kind               ├── [GAP] ⌥Tab flips to previous workroom
  ├── [GAP] ⌘Tab, ⌥⌘Tab, ⌃⌥Tab, bare Tab → nil              ├── [GAP] second tap flips back (MRU freeze)
  └── [GAP] configured modifier (Defaults) honoured         └── [GAP] [→E2E] ⌃Tab flips panes, focus lands
[+] Core/QuickSwitcherReducer.handle                        [+] Hold to reveal
  ├── [GAP] open(count<=1) → idle no-op                       ├── [GAP] rail appears after ~180ms
  ├── [GAP] open → cursor=1 / count-1, armReveal              ├── [GAP] Tab/⇧Tab + ←/→ walk the rail
  ├── [GAP] step in .pending → reveal immediately             ├── [GAP] release commits cursor card
  ├── [GAP] step in .revealed → moveCursor (wrap ±)           ├── [GAP] Esc cancels, selection unchanged
  ├── [GAP] revealTimerFired stale (not .pending) → none      ├── [GAP] hover moves cursor (REAL mouse)
  ├── [GAP] point clamped, ignored while .pending             └── [GAP] click commits (REAL mouse)
  ├── [GAP] commit(index) / commit(nil)                     [+] Cross-window
  ├── [GAP] modifierReleased on .idle → NO double commit       ├── [GAP] commit raises other window
  ├── [GAP] cancel ×4 (escape/deactivate/empty/otherKey)       ├── [GAP] modal-bearing window excluded
  └── [GAP] itemsChanged(0) end / (>0) clamp                   └── [GAP] window closes mid-session
[+] Core/SwitcherRecency (RecencyList)                      [+] Degraded previews
  ├── [GAP] touch new/existing, cap trim, forget               ├── [GAP] never-shown pane → fallback card
  ├── [GAP] retain prunes dead, preserves order                └── [GAP] capture denied → fallback card
  └── [GAP] ordered(): MRU first, untouched positional       [+] Error states
[+] Recording hooks (AppStore/WindowRegistry)                  ├── [GAP] no stuck rail: ⌥Tab then ⌘Tab away
  ├── [GAP] didSet records DURING applyLocation (A1)           └── [GAP] item dies mid-session → clamp/end
  ├── [GAP] onFocusChange records under isNavigatingHistory
  ├── [GAP] onTabsRemoved prunes pane recency
  └── [GAP] didBecomeKey records the newly-key window
[+] Item collection + commit
  ├── [GAP] excludes hasModalPresentation windows (A3)
  ├── [GAP] same-identity commit → skip (no history entry)
  ├── [GAP] dead identity → no-op
  └── [GAP] pane commit uses select (not focus)
[+] Monitor + reservation
  ├── [★★ TESTED] ⌃C reaches terminal — AppShortcutReservationTests:96
  ├── [GAP] keyCode 48 reserved for configured modifiers
  ├── [GAP] REGRESSION bare Tab never reserved
  ├── [GAP] REGRESSION ⌘↑/⌘↓ still reach handleScrollKeyEquivalent after the keyDown hoist
  ├── [GAP] ⌃Tab passthrough when <2 panes (A4)
  └── [GAP] live session swallows ⌘1-9 / ⌘W / ⌘`
[+] wrapped(index:by:count:)  ← extraction (CQ2)
  ├── [★★ TESTED] behaviour via WorkroomsViewTests (regression net)
  └── [GAP] count 0/1, negative delta, both ends
[+] Panel + rail  (PR 2)
  ├── [GAP] canBecomeKey false, .floating, .ignoresCycle
  ├── [GAP] WindowRegistry.isCycleableWindow rejects it
  ├── [GAP] badge counts from notifications.count(tab:/target:)
  └── [GAP] reduce-motion path
[+] Snapshots  (PR 2)
  ├── [GAP] cropRect: flip, scale-from-image, integral, clamp, empty→nil, 1x/2x, edge-straddle
  ├── [GAP] cache LRU by count, purge by key/window, theme-generation staleness
  ├── [GAP] service: epoch mismatch discards shot, invisible key no capture,
  │         one shot → N crops, failure keeps old entry, open bypasses debounce
  └── [GAP] registry: register/unregister, screenRect conversion, epoch bump on frame change

COVERAGE: 2/47 paths tested (4%) | Code paths: 2/32 (6%) | User flows: 0/15 (0%)
QUALITY: ★★★:0 ★★:2 ★:0 | GAPS: 45 (3 E2E, 0 eval)
```

Legend: ★★★ behavior + edge + error | ★★ happy path | ★ smoke | [→E2E] needs integration test

**REGRESSION RULE (mandatory, no decision):** two existing behaviours get modified, so regression tests are added, not offered — (1) the `isAppShortcut` hoist into `keyDown` must be proven inert for ⌘↑/⌘↓, ⌃C and bare Tab; (2) the wrap-math extraction must leave `cycleWorkroomTab`/`cycleTerminalTab` behaviour identical (`WorkroomsViewTests` is the net; add the pure-helper cases).

Now the one real test decision — three flows in that diagram are not drivable by XCUITest at all:

- Pane closed by its own process mid-session: cursor clamps or session ends
- Workroom never selected since launch: card shows the fallback glyph, not a blank thumbnail
- Theme switch (⇧⌘L) then ⌥Tab: thumbnails must not show the old theme
- Window dragged from a Retina to a non-Retina display, then ⌥Tab: crop must not be offset/scaled wrong
- App with a third-party ⌥Tab grabber running (AltTab): shortcut never arrives — verify the modifier
  preference provides a working alternative
- Screen Recording permission denied (only if the own-process capture spike fails): fallback cards,
  no repeated system prompt

## Critical paths
- ⌥Tab → hold → walk → release lands on the pictured workroom, in the right window
- ⌃Tab → hold → walk → release lands on the pictured pane, and that pane has keyboard focus
- No session can remain live: modifier release, app deactivation, Esc, and the watchdog all end it

D11 — T1: hold-to-reveal, rail hover and rail click are not drivable by XCUITest. How do we cover them? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-tests-1>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: Three of the issue's four requirements depend on things XCUITest cannot do. It cannot hold a modifier down across a sequence of events (`typeKey(_:modifierFlags:)` presses and releases per keystroke), so "hold ⌥ and the rail appears" is unreachable. And this repo has been bitten twice by synthetic input lying about hit-testing — `.textSelection` swallowing real mouseDown while synthetic clicks passed, and a hover jump that could not be reproduced without a real mouse — so a passing synthetic hover/click test on a non-key floating panel would be worse than no test: it would assert the feature works when it might not.

Stakes if we pick wrong: with the wrong plan we either ship untested reveal/commit logic, or we ship green tests that prove nothing about the panel's real mouse behaviour and find out from a user that the cards are not clickable.

Recommendation: A — make the timing and the commit decision unit-testable by injecting the clock and the reveal delay, drive the whole state machine headlessly (including "release after reveal commits exactly once"), add a `WorkroomUITestSwitcherReveal` fixture flag so an XCUITest can at least assert the rail renders, its cards exist, and a click commits, and put real-mouse hover plus hold timing on the QA checklist as explicitly manual.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=8/10.

Maps to your non-negotiable-tests preference while respecting the repo's own hard-won rule that a synthetic mouse is not evidence.

Net: everything except pixels and real-mouse physics is covered automatically, versus either trusting synthetic input or leaving the reveal path untested.

options.description:
✅ Reducer and controller take an injected clock/`Duration`, so tap-vs-hold, stale-timer, double-commit and all four cancel paths run headlessly with zero timing flake.
✅ `WorkroomUITestSwitcherReveal` (DEBUG-gated via the existing `flag()` helper) makes the rail appear on a plain keystroke so an XCUITest can assert `switcher.panel`, `switcher.card.*` and a click commit.
✅ Real-mouse hover, hold timing, and thumbnail fidelity go on the QA checklist as manual, which is honest rather than fake-green. (human: ~4h / CC: ~30min)

options.description:
✅ Smallest test surface; no fixture flag, no new UI test file, no XCUITest maintenance.
✅ Still covers every branch of the pure reducer and the recency list.
❌ Nothing automated ever proves the panel renders, that its cards are hittable, or that a commit fires from the UI — a regression in the panel wiring would ship silently.

✅ Could genuinely hold a modifier across events and post real HID-level clicks, covering the flows nothing else can.
