## Section 4 — Performance review

**[P1] (confidence: 8/10) capture allocates a full-window image per shot.** At 1:1 `pointPixelScale` a 1600×1000 window is a ~25 MB CGImage per capture, per window — then thrown away after cropping to 160×90pt cards. On a debounced activity trigger that's a 25 MB alloc + downscale every couple of seconds while a dev server logs.

**[P2] (confidence: 8/10) the trigger cadence has no "is anyone looking" gate.** Activity-settle capture only ever refreshes *visible* panes, and visible panes get re-captured at switcher-open anyway. Its one real job is keeping a pane's card fresh for the moment it becomes hidden — which means it needs a floor and a frontmost/visible gate, not a tight debounce. (Note: this partly walks back the "defer the per-window rate limiter" call from D3 — the floor is cost control, not speculation. Flagging that explicitly rather than silently reinstating it.)

**[No finding]** the recency write in `selectedTargetID.didSet` is one array move on a ≤200-element array — noise next to the `Defaults` write and status-refresh scheduling already in that observer.

questions.question:
D12 — P1: capture at 1:1 allocates ~25 MB per shot to fill a 160×90pt card. Cap the capture resolution? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-perf-1>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: The plan captures each window at full native resolution, then crops out pane rectangles and shrinks them to thumbnail size. On a Retina display a typical window is ~3200×2000 pixels — about 25 MB of image — and every byte past the thumbnail's own ~320×200 is thrown away immediately. `SCStreamConfiguration` lets us ask the compositor for a smaller image up front, and because the crop math derives its scale from the delivered image rather than from `backingScaleFactor`, a smaller image needs no other change.

Stakes if we pick wrong: at 1:1 a repeated trigger on a machine with three windows open churns tens of megabytes every couple of seconds, which shows up as memory pressure and GPU-to-CPU copy cost on a laptop — for pixels nobody ever sees.

Recommendation: A — ask for a capture whose long edge is capped around 1440px. A 160×90pt card at 2× needs 320×180 real pixels, and a pane is typically a third to a half of the window, so ~1440px across the window is already oversampled for the card.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=10/10, C=7/10 — same feature, different cost.

Maps to "engineered enough": one config field, no new abstraction, and it makes the cache's byte cap easy to respect.

Net: an image sized for the card it fills, versus a full-resolution frame discarded microseconds later.

options.label: Cap the long edge ~1440px (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Set `SCStreamConfiguration.width/height` to a scaled-down window size, roughly 1/2–1/4 the pixels, so each shot is ~2–6 MB instead of ~25 MB.
✅ Crop math is unaffected — it already derives scale from `image.width / windowOnScreen.width`, so a scaled image just yields proportionally scaled crop rects.
✅ Cheaper GPU-to-CPU transfer and less to downscale, on every trigger. (human: ~20min / CC: ~5min)

options.label: Capture 1:1, downscale after
options.description:
✅ Maximum fidelity: crop rects land on exact pixel boundaries, and a future larger card size needs no capture change.
✅ Simplest possible config — no size arithmetic at capture time.
❌ ~25 MB per shot per window, all but ~0.2 MB discarded, repeated on every activity-settle trigger — the most wasteful option for zero visible gain at card size.

options.label: Capture at exact card size
options.description:

D13 — P2: what should trigger a capture, given activity-settle only ever refreshes panes you're already looking at? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-perf-2>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: A hidden pane cannot be captured — libghostty stops rendering it — so every card for a hidden pane is a photo taken while it was last visible. That makes the trigger question sharper than it looks. Capturing when the switcher opens is free and covers everything currently on screen. Capturing "just before a pane hides" sounds ideal but cannot work: the capture is async and the plan's epoch guard would correctly throw the result away, because by the time it lands the layout has changed. Stakes if we pick wrong: too tight and a chatty dev server drives continuous capture in the background, draining battery for cards nobody opened. Too loose and ⌥Tab shows you a workroom as it looked when you arrived an hour ago, which undermines the whole point of real screenshots.

Recommendation: A — keep the settle capture, but bound it hard: only while the app is active AND the window's `occlusionState` contains `.visible`, at most once every ~3s per window, and never while a switcher session is live. ## OUTSIDE VOICE (Claude subagent — Codex timed out at 5m)

25 findings, each anchored. I re-verified the load-bearing ones myself; results noted inline in **bold**.

**Blocking / correctness**
1. `WindowRegistry.unregister` (`WindowRegistry.swift:89`) is called **only from two test files** — entries are reaped lazily by weak refs in `prune()` (`:94`), and there is no `windowWillClose` observer for the registry. So the "mandatory" snapshot purge never fires while `assignWindowNumberIfNeeded` (`:81-87`) *does* reuse a closed window's number. → give `AppStore` a `let windowToken = UUID()`; key both subsystems on it; purge hook becomes unnecessary. **Verified: `rg` finds only `RunCommandTests.swift:31` and `MultiWindowTests.swift:87`.**
2. `ObjectIdentifier(store)` has the same reclamation bug the plan rejects `windowNumber` for — it's the pointer, and a new `AppStore` at a freed address compares equal. → UUID, same fix as (1).
3. Reserving Tab in `isAppShortcut` makes the "<2 panes passes through" decision impossible; `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:990` documents the exact precedent (⌃⌘arrows deliberately *not* reserved so it passes through at a split edge). The plan's own reducer rule ("key still swallowed") contradicts the decision. → don't reserve Tab at all; consume in the monitor only when the switcher opens, like `WorkroomApp.swift:292-298`.
4. The open branch gates on the wrong predicate: `shortcutStore`/`hasModalPicker` see only `activePicker`, but `hasModalPresentation` (`AppStore.swift:586`) also covers `auxSheetPresented`, `pendingCommit`, `pendingDeletion`, `pendingProjectSettings`, `pendingRemoteConfirm`… → gate on `hasModalPresentation`. **Verified — that property lists all of those.**
5. Hoisting `isAppShortcut` to the *top* of `keyDown` is not behaviour-preserving: the `onCloseRequested` "press any key to close" guard at `:834` currently runs first. → insert after `:837`. (Rest of the claim confirmed: the reservation is genuinely dead for non-⌘ keys today.)
6. Build order 3 can't commit without step 4 — commit happens on modifier release, which step 4 introduces. → step 3 commits immediately per keyDown; step 4 *changes* commit timing (a semantic change, not an increment).
7. Tab autorepeat is never filtered; holding Tab steps ~15×/sec. macOS ⌘Tab ignores repeats. → `guard !event.isARepeat`.
8. ⌥Tab/⌃Tab in the quick terminal become silently dead keys (`shortcutStore(for:)` is nil for `QuickTerminalWindow`, `:106`, but the branch always returns nil). → return `event` when there's no workroom store.

**Screenshots**
9. Cut the capture subsystem; the plan's own plan B is strictly better. `readCommandRegion` (`:777`) reads the terminal *state machine*, which keeps running for hidden panes (occlusion pauses only rendering) — so text is **live** where a screenshot is structurally frozen, works for never-visited panes, and needs no TCC, epoch, LRU, rect reporter or `project.yml` change. At 160×90 a downscaled terminal is illegible mush, carrying near-zero information over title + glyph + badge. → ship the fallback card plus 2–3 lines of `readCommandRegion` text; delete ~7 files and both mount points.
10. `pointPixelScale` and `contentRect` are **readonly on the filter** (`SCStream.h:114`, `:119`); config offers only `width`/`height`/`scalesToFit` (`:212`, `:217`, `:239`). A long-edge cap with a non-matching aspect letterboxes and misaligns the crop. → size strictly proportional to `contentRect`, compute scaleX *and* scaleY, assert they match. **Verified in the header.**
11. `currentProcess` content is documented as *redacted* — `windowID` matching is fine, `title`/`owningApplication` may be nil. The no-TCC *read* is supported; the no-TCC *capture* is still inference. → spike must assert a real `CGImage` with non-uniform pixels.
12. The first SCK capture initializes the subsystem (hundreds of ms) and loses the 180 ms race, so the first hold shows fallback cards that then pop. A window on an inactive Space can also return an all-black *successful* capture. → warm at idle; skip `!isOnActiveSpace`.

**Modifier release**
13. Drop the flagsChanged monitor; the watchdog alone is correct and simpler. `NSEvent.modifierFlags` is a global hardware snapshot that survives menu tracking, Mission Control and Spaces — and Mission Control posts no `didResignActive`, so of the four mitigations only the poll covers it. → one 30 ms poll while live; delete the monitor and its return-event invariant.
14. Sticky Keys clears the ⌥ latch on the first non-modifier key, so hold can never be reached; no API detects it. → accept, document, ensure a <30 ms release still commits.
15. "⌥Tab is safe" is wrong at the app layer — AltTab, HyperSwitch, Contexts bind it by default via CGEvent taps, upstream of `NSApp.sendEvent`. → the `Defaults` trigger from day one (agrees with A5).
16. A configurable modifier collides with `isAppShortcut`/`classify` static purity. → (3) removes Tab from `isAppShortcut` anyway; pass configured modifiers into `classify` as a parameter.
17. All-windows commit can trigger a Space/full-screen switch animation (~0.5–1 s), so "instant flip" isn't. → scope to current Space by default, or note it.

**Panel**
18. Hover/clicks work, but for a different reason: `.onHover` uses `.activeInActiveApp` tracking areas (app is active mid-shortcut); `acceptsFirstMouse` only matters when the app is inactive. **Occlusion: no impact** — `occlusionState` counts only *opaque* coverage and the panel is clear. → assert the panel stays non-opaque, or terminal rendering stops behind it.
19. `QuickTerminalWindow` is a plain `NSWindow` with `.titled` (`QuickTerminalController.swift:7`, `:100`) — no precedent for `canBecomeKey == false` / `.nonactivatingPanel`. Only the `.themeDidChange` observer (`:118`) is reusable. Lazy creation also pays first-`NSHostingView` render at reveal. → pre-create at launch, ordered out.

**Smaller**
20. The "180 ms matches `EdgeRevealSidebar`" precedent is a misread — `:127` is a *hide* debounce; that reveal is immediate. 180 ms also flashes on a chorded tap. → default ~250 ms, one constant.
21. `revealWorkroom` is unnecessary (agrees with CQ1); plan file is stale. → `store.hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil); store.openExisting(sid)`.
22. `fullTitle` is already duplicated at `WorkroomTabBar.swift:460` and `WorkroomSplitView.swift:437`; the rail makes three. And `RootPresentation.make` returns a *branch name*, not a workroom label (`Models.swift:136-158`). → hoist one `label(for: SidebarID)` onto `AppStore`. **Verified both.**
23. The wrap-math extraction is make-work — the two cyclers differ materially and share one line. → skip.

**Strategic**
24. PR1 alone ships a blind switcher plus a regression: hold-and-step with no rail moves an invisible cursor, strictly worse than today's ⇧⌥⌘←/→ which acts per press, while ⌃Tab is taken from TUIs immediately. → PR1 = tap-only, immediate commit, no hold path.
25. This is navigation mechanism #5 and #6, and the rail duplicates ⌘O (which already answers "what's open", with search and no capture). The unmet need is one keystroke of MRU. → land the MRU tap, add MRU ordering to the ⌘O picker, build the rail only if the tap proves insufficient — ~2 files instead of 9 for most of the value.

**CROSS-MODEL TENSION**
- **Preview fidelity (#9, #25):** you chose real screenshots; the outside voice argues text previews are *live* for hidden panes where screenshots are frozen, and that at card size a terminal thumbnail is illegible. Both are true. What I might be missing: how big your cards actually are — at 220×140 a screenshot reads fine, at 160×90 it doesn't.
- **Wrap extraction (#23):** review said extract (you approved, CQ2); outside voice says make-work. Your call stands unless you say otherwise — I'm not re-arguing it.
- **Window identity (#1/#2):** the outside voice is right and my A2 recommendation was weaker — `ObjectIdentifier` can alias a freed address. Same decision, better token: UUID.
- **⌃Tab reservation (#3):** the outside voice resolves the exact contradiction I flagged as A4's downside, by deleting the reservation instead of conditionalizing it.

**Folding without a question** (no tradeoff, or already-decided): 1, 2 (UUID token), 4 (gate on `hasModalPresentation`), 7 (`isARepeat`), 8 (pass through when no store), 10 (proportional capture + scale assert), 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 (250 ms), 21, 22 (`label(for:)` helper).

Four need your call. First:

questions.question:
D17 — OV4: how should modifier release be detected — poll only, or the flagsChanged monitor plus poll? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-ov-release-detect>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`, issue #132 plan.

ELI10: In PR2 the rail commits when you let go of ⌥ or ⌃. Two ways to notice that. A local `flagsChanged` monitor sees the release event — but only while the app is receiving events, so menu tracking, Mission Control and another app taking focus all starve it, and Mission Control notably posts no `didResignActive` either. The other way is to poll `NSEvent.modifierFlags`, a global hardware snapshot that is true regardless of who has focus. The plan wanted both: monitor as the fast path, poll as the safety net. The outside voice argues the poll alone is correct AND simpler, because it also removes a hazard the plan itself flagged: the monitor must always return the event, or `GhosttySurfaceView.flagsChanged` (:927) leaves libghostty believing ⌥ is still held.

Stakes if we pick wrong: keep both and you carry a component whose only job is latency, plus a return-the-event invariant that will eventually be violated by someone refactoring the monitor — and a stuck-⌥ terminal is a nasty bug. Poll only, and commit lands up to one poll interval late.

Recommendation: A — poll only, at 30 ms. That's below the ~50–100 ms threshold where a release feels delayed, it covers every starvation case including Mission Control, and it deletes a whole event path plus its invariant. Keep `didResignActive` as a cancel trigger since it's one line and semantically distinct (you left the app; don't commit).

Completeness: A=10/10, B=10/10, C=7/10 — same coverage, different mechanism count.

Maps to "engineered enough" and systems-over-heroes: one mechanism that cannot be starved beats two where the fast one has a footgun.

Net: one unstarvable poll with a hair of latency, versus two paths where the fast one can leave a modifier stuck in the terminal.

options.label: 30ms poll only (recommended)
options.description:
✅ `NSEvent.modifierFlags` is hardware truth, so it works through menu tracking, Mission Control, Spaces and focus loss — the cases that starve a local monitor.
✅ Deletes the flagsChanged monitor and its must-always-return-the-event invariant, so no refactor can leave libghostty thinking ⌥ is held.
✅ One timing mechanism to test, driven by the injected clock from T1. (human: ~1h saved / CC: ~10min saved)
❌ Commit can land up to 30 ms after release, and a poll runs for the whole session — trivial, but it is busywork where an event would be exact.

options.label: Monitor + poll as planned
options.description:
✅ Exact, zero-latency commit in the common case, with the poll catching the starvation cases.
✅ Matches how the rest of the app handles keys — event-driven first, which is the familiar shape for a reader.
❌ Two mechanisms for one signal, and the monitor carries a footgun: swallow the ⌥ release once and the terminal is left with a phantom held modifier until the next flags change.

options.label: Poll at 100ms
options.description:
✅ Cheapest possible: a tenth the wakeups of the 30 ms version, still no monitor and no invariant.
✅ Plenty fast for cancel/teardown safety.
❌ 100 ms after release is perceptible on the commit — the rail lingers after your thumb is off the key, which is exactly the kind of lag that makes a switcher feel worse than the OS one it imitates.

input.content:
# Issue #132 — Terminal/Workroom quick switcher (⌥Tab / ⌃Tab)

## Context

Workroom's navigation is entirely positional: ⌥⌘←/→ steps terminal tabs, ⇧⌥⌘←/→ steps workroom
tabs, ⌘1–9 / ⌥⌘1–9 jump by index, ⌘` cycles windows, ⌘[/] walks history. Nothing flips you back to
*what you were just looking at*, and nothing shows what's open without reading the tab bars.

Issue #132 asks for the macOS ⌘Tab experience, twice: **⌥Tab** for open workrooms across all app
windows, **⌃Tab** for the current workroom's detail panes. Quick tap switches immediately;
press-and-hold shows a screen-centred rail of screenshot thumbnails with labels and notification
badges; arrows/hover/click walk it; release commits.

Decisions taken with the user, then hardened through an engineering review + outside voice:
real screenshots (not text previews), MRU ordering, a floating panel so the rail can span windows,
all-windows scope, and **two shipped stages** — PR1 is tap-only and complete on its own, PR2 adds
hold-to-reveal and moves the commit to modifier release.

---

## Stage 1 (PR1) — tap-only MRU switching

No panel, no reducer, no release detection. Every ⌥Tab / ⌃Tab press commits immediately, exactly
like today's arrow cycling but ordered by recency. Ships as a complete sentence: "⌥Tab flips to the
workroom you were just in."

### Key routing

```
keyDown event
  │
  ├─ ⌘W branches (quick terminal, aux window)          ← unchanged, must stay first
  ├─ window = event.window ?? NSApp.keyWindow           ← unchanged
  ├─ ⌘` / ⇧⌘` window cycle                             ← unchanged
  │
  ├─ NEW: QuickSwitcherKey.classify(keyCode:flags:modifiers:) → .workrooms/.panes/nil
  │     │   keyCode 48 (Tab); modifiers come from Defaults (⌥ / ⌃ by default)
  │     ├─ event.isARepeat ................................ return nil  (swallow, don't spin)
  │     ├─ no store for `window` (quick terminal, Settings) return event (terminal keeps ⌃Tab)
  │     ├─ store.hasModalPresentation ..................... return nil  (swallow behind a sheet)
  │     ├─ switcher committed a switch .................... return nil
  │     └─ nothing to switch to (<2 items) ................ return event (⌃Tab reaches the TUI)
  │
  └─ existing ⌘1-9 / ⌥⌘1-9 / ⌘R / arrows / sidebar branches … → return event
```

Three things this deliberately does **not** do:
- **No `isAppShortcut` change and no `keyDown` hoist.** A static allowlist can't express "pass
  through when there's nothing to switch to", and the codebase already chose that side of the fork:
  ⌃⌘arrows is "deliberately **NOT** reserved — it passes through to the terminal at a split's edge"
  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989-990`). The monitor runs inside `NSApp.sendEvent` before dispatch, so
  when the switcher *does* act the surface never sees the key. Hoisting the classifier into `keyDown`
  would also have to land after the `onCloseRequested` "press any key to close" guard (`:834`) or it
  breaks run-pane closing — another reason not to touch that file.
- **No `flagsChanged` monitor** (nothing to detect in PR1).
- **No unconditional swallow.** Aux/quick-terminal windows and single-item cases return the event.

Gate on `store.hasModalPresentation` (`AppStore.swift:586`), **not** `activePicker`: the latter
misses `auxSheetPresented`, `pendingCommit`, `pendingDeletion`, `pendingProjectSettings`,
`pendingRemoteConfirm`, so ⌥Tab could otherwise retarget the selection under an open commit sheet.

### MRU

`Core/SwitcherRecency.swift`:

```swift
struct RecencyList<ID: Hashable> {                    // pure value type
  mutating func touch(_ id: ID); mutating func forget(_ id: ID); mutating func retain(_ live: Set<ID>)
  func ordered<T>(_ items: [T], id: (T) -> ID) -> [T] // MRU first, never-touched appended positionally
}
struct WindowToken: Hashable { let raw: UUID }         // AppStore.windowToken — NEVER reused
struct WorkroomSlotID: Hashable { let window: WindowToken; let sid: SidebarID }

@MainActor final class SwitcherRecency {
  static let shared = SwitcherRecency()
  func recordWorkroom(store: AppStore, sid: SidebarID?); func recordPane(_ id: TerminalTab.ID)
  func forgetPanes(_ ids: [TerminalTab.ID])
  func workroomOrder(_ slots: [WorkroomSlot]) -> [WorkroomSlot]
  func paneOrder(_ tabs: [TerminalTab]) -> [TerminalTab]
```

**Window identity is `let windowToken = UUID()` on `AppStore`** — not `windowNumber` (reclaimed by
`assignWindowNumberIfNeeded`, `WindowRegistry.swift:81-87`) and not `ObjectIdentifier(store)` (a
pointer; a new store at a freed address compares equal). `windowNumber` stays what it already is: the
`"Window \(n)"` display string (`AppStore.swift:1068`). This also means the snapshot cache needs no
purge-on-window-close hook to be *correct* — which matters, because `WindowRegistry.unregister`
(`:89`) has **no production caller** (only `RunCommandTests.swift:31` and `MultiWindowTests.swift:87`;
entries are reaped lazily by weak refs in `prune()`, `:94`).

Recording hooks — **all unconditional, above the `isNavigatingHistory` guard**:

| Hook | Site | Why unconditional |
|---|---|---|
| `recordWorkroom(store:sid:)` | `AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet` (`:157`) | `applyLocation` raises `isNavigatingHistory` for its whole body (`:3703`), and the switcher commits through it — a gated write would never fire |
| `recordWorkroom` | `WindowRegistry`'s existing `didBecomeKey` observer (`:48`) | without it, ⌘` to another window leaves MRU[0] on the window you left |
| `recordPane(tabID)` | `AppStore`'s `terminals.onFocusChange` (`:828`) | same suppression (`:836`); recency ≠ history |
| `forgetPanes(ids)` | `terminals.onTabsRemoved` (`:843`) | prune closed panes |

Panes key on `TerminalTab.ID` alone (a UUID, unique app-wide). Recency is in-memory/session-scoped.

```swift

WindowRegistry.shared.allStores
```

```swift
store.hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)     // precedent: AppStore.swift:1972
```

**No new AppStore method.** `openExisting(_:)` (`:3775`) already *is* "select a workroom, restore its

## Stage 2 (PR2) — hold-to-reveal rail

Introduces the reducer, the panel, the rail and capture, and **changes commit timing from
press to modifier release** — an intentional behaviour change, called out in the PR body.

### Session state machine

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────── cancel(escape|deactivated|empty) ──────┐
                    │                                                                    ▼
   idle ──open(count>1)──▶ pending ──revealTimerFired(250ms)──▶ revealed ──modifierReleased──▶ idle
    ▲  │                     │  │                                 │  ▲                        │
    │  └─open(count<=1)──▶ idle  └──step──▶ revealed (immediate)   │  └─point/step (wrap ±)    │
    │                                                              └──commit(index) ───────────┘
    └──────────── every event while .idle is a no-op ◀── (click commit then modifier release)
```

`Core/QuickSwitcherReducer.swift`, in the shape of `EdgeRevealReducer`
(`Views/EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:30`):

```swift
enum Event { case open(kind:count:reverse:), step(reverse:), point(index:), revealTimerFired,
             commit(index: Int?), modifierReleased, cancel(Cancel), itemsChanged(count: Int) }
enum Effect { case none, armReveal, reveal, moveCursor(Int), end(commit: Int?) }
mutating func handle(_ event: Event) -> Effect
```

Load-bearing rules: `.idle` swallows everything (so a click commit followed by the inevitable
modifier release can't double-commit); `.step` while `.pending` reveals immediately (⌘Tab⌘Tab);
`revealTimerFired` outside `.pending` is a no-op (stale timer after a fast release);
`itemsChanged(0)` ends without commit, `>0` clamps. Reveal delay **250 ms**, one injected constant —
180 ms flashes on a chorded tap, and the "matches `EdgeRevealSidebar`" precedent was a misread (that
180 ms is a *hide* debounce at `:127`).

### Release detection — poll only

One 30 ms poll of `NSEvent.modifierFlags` while a session is live. It's a global hardware snapshot,
so it survives menu tracking, Mission Control and another app holding focus — the cases that starve a
local monitor, and Mission Control posts no `didResignActive` either. **No `flagsChanged` monitor**:
it would only buy latency, and it carries a real footgun (it must always `return event` or
`GhosttySurfaceView.flagsChanged`, `:927`, leaves libghostty believing ⌥ is still held).

Also live: `didResignActive` → cancel (you left the app, don't commit); `willClose` → re-resolve items
→ `itemsChanged`; Escape → cancel; a hard 10 s ceiling. Sticky Keys clears the ⌥ latch on the first
non-modifier key, so hold is unreachable for those users and the feature degrades to single-step flip
— documented, not worked around (no API detects it).

### Panel

`Core/SwitcherPanel.swift` — first `NSPanel` in the app. `QuickTerminalWindow` is **not** a
precedent (it's a plain `.titled NSWindow`, `QuickTerminalController.swift:7`, `:100`); only its
`.themeDidChange` observer (`:118`) is reusable.

```swift
final class SwitcherPanel: NSPanel {
  override var canBecomeKey: Bool { false }      // key stays with the workroom window → monitor keeps working
  override var canBecomeMain: Bool { false }
}
```

`[.nonactivatingPanel, .borderless]`, `isFloatingPanel = true`, `level = .floating`,
`collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .ignoresCycle, .transient]`,
`isOpaque = false`, `backgroundColor = .clear`, `hasShadow = false`, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`,
`isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true`, `animationBehavior = .none`, a11y id `switcher.panel`.

- **Pre-create at launch, ordered out** — lazy creation pays first-`NSHostingView` render cost at the
  250 ms reveal.
- **`isOpaque = false` is load-bearing and gets a test.** `NSWindow.occlusionState` counts only
  *opaque* coverage, so a clear panel never flips it and `GhosttySurfaceView`'s occlusion path
  (`:441`, `:384`) never fires. Give the panel an opaque background later and terminal rendering
  stops behind it.
- ⌘` ignores it twice: `WindowRegistry.isCycleableWindow` (`:151`) requires `canBecomeKey`, plus
  `.ignoresCycle`. Drop `private` from that method so a test can assert it.
- Mouse works because `.onHover` uses `.activeInActiveApp` tracking areas and the app *is* active
  mid-shortcut; `acceptsFirstMouse` only matters when the app is inactive.
- Never `addChildWindow` it — `SCStreamConfiguration.includeChildWindows` defaults true and the panel
  would contaminate captures.
- Placement: centred in the key window's screen `visibleFrame`, recomputed per open.
- Panel touches no `AppStore`; the controller feeds value-type `SwitcherCard`s into
  `SwitcherRailModel` (`items`, `cursor`, `themeVersion`, `onHover`, `onCommit`).

**Invariant (prior learning `macapp-row-observes-sessions-invalidation-storm`):** no rail view may
hold an `AppStore` or `TerminalSessions`. `TerminalSessions` republishes per title/activity pulse; a
card observing it to compute "is cursor" would re-run at OSC frequency — the WORKROOM-2B hang.

### Rail

`Views/SwitcherRailView.swift` — horizontal `ScrollView` + `ScrollViewReader`, `HStack(spacing: 12)`,
`.sidebarCard(cornerRadius: 16, margin: 0, elevated: true)`, revealed with
`DialogOverlayStyle.revealAnimation`, `.scrollTo(cursor, anchor: .center)`, and a
`@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` snap path.

Card ≈ **220×140** (≈440×280 real px) — at 160×90 a downscaled terminal is illegible mush, which was
the outside voice's strongest argument against screenshots at all.
- thumbnail, or — when no snapshot exists — a **live text preview**: 2–3 tidied lines from
  `GhosttySurfaceView.readCommandRegion(maxBytes: 2_048)` (`:777`) + `TerminalCapture.tidy`, in the
  terminal font over `tokens.bg`. This is live even for hidden panes (occlusion stops rendering, not
  the terminal state machine) and needs no permission — it covers exactly what capture can't: a pane
  never visible this launch. Content panes fall back to their kind glyph (`plusminus` / `doc` /
  `clock`).
- title + subtitle from `AppStore.label(for:)`; `"Window \(windowNumber)"` as subtitle when one
  `SidebarID` appears in two windows.
- `UnreadBadge(count:)` top-trailing from `notifications.count(target:)` / `count(tab:)`.
- running dot from `TerminalTab.isRunning` / `terminals.isRunning(forTargetID:)`.
- cursor ring `strokeBorder(tokens.accent, lineWidth: 2)`; a11y ids `switcher.rail`,
  `switcher.card.<label>`.
- Text previews are synchronous main-thread libghostty reads: cursor ±3 only, lazily as the cursor
  moves, never from inside a libghostty callback.

### Capture

Own-process capture, verified in the SDK header (`SCShareableContent.h:151`):
`SCShareableContent.currentProcess` (macOS 14.4+) returns content "available to capture by current
process **without user consent via TCC**" — but the content is documented as *redacted*, so match on
`windowID` (`title`/`owningApplication` may be nil), and the no-TCC *capture* is still inference.
**Day-0 spike:** revoke Screen Recording for `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, capture our own
window, and assert a real `CGImage` **with non-uniform pixels** — not merely a non-nil filter.

One window capture per shot, N crops:

```swift
let scWindow = content.windows.first { $0.windowID == CGWindowID(nsWindow.windowNumber) }
let filter = SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow: scWindow)     // ignores overlapping windows
// size: s = min(1, 1440 / max(contentRect.width, contentRect.height) * pointPixelScale-adjusted)
config.width  = Int((filter.contentRect.width  * scale).rounded())
config.height = Int((filter.contentRect.height * scale).rounded())   // STRICTLY proportional
config.showsCursor = false
config.ignoreShadowsSingleWindow = true
config.ignoreGlobalClipSingleWindow = true
let image = try await SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: filter, configuration: config)
```

`pointPixelScale` and `contentRect` are **readonly on the filter** (`SCStream.h:114`, `:119`); the
config exposes only `width`/`height`/`scalesToFit` (`:212`, `:217`, `:239`). A long-edge cap with a
non-matching aspect letterboxes and silently misaligns every crop — so size proportionally, derive
**both** scaleX and scaleY from the delivered image, and assert they match.

Gate on `nsWindow.isVisible && !nsWindow.isMiniaturized && nsWindow.isOnActiveSpace` (a window on an
inactive Space can return an all-black *successful* image, which "keep the old entry on failure"
would not catch). Warm the SCK path once at idle — the first call initializes the subsystem for
hundreds of ms and would otherwise lose the 250 ms reveal race on the very first hold.

```
 request                                 resume
 ───────                                 ──────
 read epoch, window.frame,      ──▶ await capture ──▶  epoch changed? ──yes──▶ DISCARD whole shot
 and every visible region's                            frame changed? ──yes──▶ DISCARD
 screen rect (synchronously)                                  │no
                                                              ▼
                                              crop planned rects → downscale → cache
```

The epoch guard makes a mislabeled card structurally impossible; worst case is a stale one. Crop math
is pure and testable — both rects live in the same y-up screen space (`view.convert(bounds, to: nil)`
→ `window.convertToScreen`), so the global flip cancels: no `NSScreen` lookup, no multi-display case.

```swift
enum SnapshotKey: Hashable { case pane(TerminalTab.ID), workroom(SidebarID, WindowToken) }
enum SnapshotGeometry {
  static func cropRect(regionOnScreen: CGRect, windowOnScreen: CGRect, imagePixelSize: CGSize) -> CGRect?
  static func thumbnailPixelSize(source: CGSize, maxPointWidth: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat) -> CGSize
}
```

Triggers — switcher-open (immediate, unbounded, fired **before** the panel is ordered in);
became-visible; activity-settled, gated on app-active **and** the window's `occlusionState`
containing `.visible`, at most once per ~3 s per window, never while a session is live; and
**theme change** (also bumps `themeGeneration`, so older entries read stale). No resize trigger — a
resize bumps the epoch, so no stale in-flight crop lands and the next natural capture fixes the card.
Honest limit: libghostty exposes no damage signal, so a shell producing output with no OSC won't
refresh between triggers; the escalation is a fork-side damage callback, not a tighter timer.

Cache: LRU, `maxEntries = 32`, byte cap, injected clock. Purge on `onTabsRemoved` and workroom
deletion. Rects come from a zero-drawing `SnapshotRectReporter` (`Views/`) registered in
`SnapshotRegistry`, mounted `.background { }` at exactly two always-mounted sites: `PaneLeafView`
(`Views/PaneTreeView.swift:383`, covers all four `TabContent` kinds) and `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:164`, covers solo *and* split since `RootView.workroomSplitBody`
always renders through `WorkroomSplitView`).

If the spike shows TCC *is* required: `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` for status (never prompt at
launch), `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` only from an explicit in-rail affordance, deep-link to
`x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture`, re-preflight on
`didBecomeActive`, and `Defaults[.railPreviews]` to opt out. Screen Recording needs no entitlement and
no Info.plist key; keep `CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS: NO` (`project.yml:299`). Add
`- sdk: ScreenCaptureKit.framework` to `project.yml`.

# Issue #132 — Terminal/Workroom quick switcher (⌥Tab / ⌃Tab)

## Context

Workroom's navigation is entirely positional: ⌥⌘←/→ steps terminal tabs, ⇧⌥⌘←/→ steps workroom
tabs, ⌘1–9 / ⌥⌘1–9 jump by index, ⌘` cycles windows, ⌘[/] walks history. Nothing flips you back to
*what you were just looking at*, and nothing shows what's open without reading the tab bars.

Issue #132 asks for the macOS ⌘Tab experience, twice: **⌥Tab** for open workrooms across all app
windows, **⌃Tab** for the current workroom's detail panes. Quick tap switches immediately;
press-and-hold shows a screen-centred rail of screenshot thumbnails with labels and notification
badges; arrows/hover/click walk it; release commits.

Decisions taken with the user, then hardened through an engineering review + outside voice:
real screenshots (not text previews), MRU ordering, a floating panel so the rail can span windows,
all-windows scope, and **two shipped stages** — PR1 is tap-only and complete on its own, PR2 adds
hold-to-reveal and moves the commit to modifier release.

---

## Stage 1 (PR1) — tap-only MRU switching

No panel, no reducer, no release detection. Every ⌥Tab / ⌃Tab press commits immediately, exactly
like today's arrow cycling but ordered by recency. Ships as a complete sentence: "⌥Tab flips to the
workroom you were just in."

### Key routing

```
keyDown event
  │
  ├─ ⌘W branches (quick terminal, aux window)          ← unchanged, must stay first
  ├─ window = event.window ?? NSApp.keyWindow           ← unchanged
  ├─ ⌘` / ⇧⌘` window cycle                             ← unchanged
  │
  ├─ NEW: QuickSwitcherKey.classify(keyCode:flags:modifiers:) → .workrooms/.panes/nil
  │     │   keyCode 48 (Tab); modifiers come from Defaults (⌥ / ⌃ by default)
  │     ├─ event.isARepeat ................................ return nil  (swallow, don't spin)
  │     ├─ no store for `window` (quick terminal, Settings) return event (terminal keeps ⌃Tab)
  │     ├─ store.hasModalPresentation ..................... return nil  (swallow behind a sheet)
  │     ├─ switcher committed a switch .................... return nil
  │     └─ nothing to switch to (<2 items) ................ return event (⌃Tab reaches the TUI)
  │
  └─ existing ⌘1-9 / ⌥⌘1-9 / ⌘R / arrows / sidebar branches … → return event
```

Three things this deliberately does **not** do:
- **No `isAppShortcut` change and no `keyDown` hoist.** A static allowlist can't express "pass
  through when there's nothing to switch to", and the codebase already chose that side of the fork:
  ⌃⌘arrows is "deliberately **NOT** reserved — it passes through to the terminal at a split's edge"
  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989-990`). The monitor runs inside `NSApp.sendEvent` before dispatch, so
  when the switcher *does* act the surface never sees the key. Hoisting the classifier into `keyDown`
  would also have to land after the `onCloseRequested` "press any key to close" guard (`:834`) or it
  breaks run-pane closing — another reason not to touch that file.
- **No `flagsChanged` monitor** (nothing to detect in PR1).
- **No unconditional swallow.** Aux/quick-terminal windows and single-item cases return the event.

Gate on `store.hasModalPresentation` (`AppStore.swift:586`), **not** `activePicker`: the latter
misses `auxSheetPresented`, `pendingCommit`, `pendingDeletion`, `pendingProjectSettings`,
`pendingRemoteConfirm`, so ⌥Tab could otherwise retarget the selection under an open commit sheet.

### MRU

`Core/SwitcherRecency.swift`:

```swift
struct RecencyList<ID: Hashable> {                    // pure value type
  mutating func touch(_ id: ID); mutating func forget(_ id: ID); mutating func retain(_ live: Set<ID>)
  func ordered<T>(_ items: [T], id: (T) -> ID) -> [T] // MRU first, never-touched appended positionally
}
struct WindowToken: Hashable { let raw: UUID }         // AppStore.windowToken — NEVER reused
struct WorkroomSlotID: Hashable { let window: WindowToken; let sid: SidebarID }

@MainActor final class SwitcherRecency {
  static let shared = SwitcherRecency()
  func recordWorkroom(store: AppStore, sid: SidebarID?); func recordPane(_ id: TerminalTab.ID)
  func forgetPanes(_ ids: [TerminalTab.ID])
  func workroomOrder(_ slots: [WorkroomSlot]) -> [WorkroomSlot]
  func paneOrder(_ tabs: [TerminalTab]) -> [TerminalTab]
}
```

**Window identity is `let windowToken = UUID()` on `AppStore`** — not `windowNumber` (reclaimed by
`assignWindowNumberIfNeeded`, `WindowRegistry.swift:81-87`) and not `ObjectIdentifier(store)` (a
pointer; a new store at a freed address compares equal). `windowNumber` stays what it already is: the
`"Window \(n)"` display string (`AppStore.swift:1068`). This also means the snapshot cache needs no
purge-on-window-close hook to be *correct* — which matters, because `WindowRegistry.unregister`
(`:89`) has **no production caller** (only `RunCommandTests.swift:31` and `MultiWindowTests.swift:87`;
entries are reaped lazily by weak refs in `prune()`, `:94`).

Recording hooks — **all unconditional, above the `isNavigatingHistory` guard**:

| Hook | Site | Why unconditional |
|---|---|---|
| `recordWorkroom(store:sid:)` | `AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet` (`:157`) | `applyLocation` raises `isNavigatingHistory` for its whole body (`:3703`), and the switcher commits through it — a gated write would never fire |
| `recordWorkroom` | `WindowRegistry`'s existing `didBecomeKey` observer (`:48`) | without it, ⌘` to another window leaves MRU[0] on the window you left |
| `recordPane(tabID)` | `AppStore`'s `terminals.onFocusChange` (`:828`) | same suppression (`:836`); recency ≠ history |
| `forgetPanes(ids)` | `terminals.onTabsRemoved` (`:843`) | prune closed panes |

Panes key on `TerminalTab.ID` alone (a UUID, unique app-wide). Recency is in-memory/session-scoped.

### Item collection + commit

```swift
// workrooms: every window, MRU-ordered, frozen per press
WindowRegistry.shared.allStores
  .filter { !$0.hasModalPresentation }                  // can't switch into a busy window
  .flatMap { store in store.displayedWorkroomTargets().map { WorkroomSlot(store: store, …) } }
// panes: the key window's selected target only
store.terminals.tabs(for: target)
```

Commit, in this order (raise **first** — `persistsSidebarPrefs` keys on `lastActiveStore === self`,
`AppStore.swift:140`):

```swift
if !NSApp.isActive { NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true) }
store.hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)     // precedent: AppStore.swift:1972
store.openExisting(sid)                          // = NSApp.activate + applyLocation(target:tab:nil, recordHistory:true)
// panes:
store.terminals.select(tabID, for: target)       // `select`, not `focus` — fires onSurfaceFocused
```

**No new AppStore method.** `openExisting(_:)` (`:3775`) already *is* "select a workroom, restore its
focused tab, record one history entry". Skip the whole commit when the chosen identity is already
current: no raise, no write, no history entry (so ⌘[ isn't spammed).

### Shared wrap math

Extract `(current + step + count) % count` — written verbatim at `AppStore.swift:1156` and `:3444` —
into one pure `nonisolated static func wrapped(index:by:count:)`, reuse it in both cyclers and in the
switcher's MRU step. Existing coverage in `WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomsViewTests.swift` is the
regression net. (The outside voice called this make-work since the two cyclers differ in their
entry-when-absent behaviour; the user's call stands.)

### Label DRY

`fullTitle` is already duplicated at `WorkroomTabBar.swift:460` and `WorkroomSplitView.swift:437`;
the rail would be the third. Hoist one `AppStore.label(for: SidebarID) -> String` and have all three
read it. Note `RootPresentation.make` returns a **branch name**, not a workroom label
(`Models.swift:136-158`) — a root card must not use it as a title.

---

## Stage 2 (PR2) — hold-to-reveal rail

Introduces the reducer, the panel, the rail and capture, and **changes commit timing from
press to modifier release** — an intentional behaviour change, called out in the PR body.

### Session state machine

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────── cancel(escape|deactivated|empty) ──────┐
                    │                                                                    ▼
   idle ──open(count>1)──▶ pending ──revealTimerFired(250ms)──▶ revealed ──modifierReleased──▶ idle
    ▲  │                     │  │                                 │  ▲                        │
    │  └─open(count<=1)──▶ idle  └──step──▶ revealed (immediate)   │  └─point/step (wrap ±)    │
    │                                                              └──commit(index) ───────────┘
    └──────────── every event while .idle is a no-op ◀── (click commit then modifier release)
```

`Core/QuickSwitcherReducer.swift`, in the shape of `EdgeRevealReducer`
(`Views/EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:30`):

```swift
enum Event { case open(kind:count:reverse:), step(reverse:), point(index:), revealTimerFired,
             commit(index: Int?), modifierReleased, cancel(Cancel), itemsChanged(count: Int) }
enum Effect { case none, armReveal, reveal, moveCursor(Int), end(commit: Int?) }
mutating func handle(_ event: Event) -> Effect
```

Load-bearing rules: `.idle` swallows everything (so a click commit followed by the inevitable
modifier release can't double-commit); `.step` while `.pending` reveals immediately (⌘Tab⌘Tab);
`revealTimerFired` outside `.pending` is a no-op (stale timer after a fast release);
`itemsChanged(0)` ends without commit, `>0` clamps. Reveal delay **250 ms**, one injected constant —
180 ms flashes on a chorded tap, and the "matches `EdgeRevealSidebar`" precedent was a misread (that
180 ms is a *hide* debounce at `:127`).

### Release detection — poll only

One 30 ms poll of `NSEvent.modifierFlags` while a session is live. It's a global hardware snapshot,
so it survives menu tracking, Mission Control and another app holding focus — the cases that starve a
local monitor, and Mission Control posts no `didResignActive` either. **No `flagsChanged` monitor**:
it would only buy latency, and it carries a real footgun (it must always `return event` or
`GhosttySurfaceView.flagsChanged`, `:927`, leaves libghostty believing ⌥ is still held).

Also live: `didResignActive` → cancel (you left the app, don't commit); `willClose` → re-resolve items
→ `itemsChanged`; Escape → cancel; a hard 10 s ceiling. Sticky Keys clears the ⌥ latch on the first
non-modifier key, so hold is unreachable for those users and the feature degrades to single-step flip
— documented, not worked around (no API detects it).

### Panel

`Core/SwitcherPanel.swift` — first `NSPanel` in the app. `QuickTerminalWindow` is **not** a
precedent (it's a plain `.titled NSWindow`, `QuickTerminalController.swift:7`, `:100`); only its
`.themeDidChange` observer (`:118`) is reusable.

```swift
final class SwitcherPanel: NSPanel {
  override var canBecomeKey: Bool { false }      // key stays with the workroom window → monitor keeps working
  override var canBecomeMain: Bool { false }
}
```

`[.nonactivatingPanel, .borderless]`, `isFloatingPanel = true`, `level = .floating`,
`collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .ignoresCycle, .transient]`,
`isOpaque = false`, `backgroundColor = .clear`, `hasShadow = false`, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`,
`isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true`, `animationBehavior = .none`, a11y id `switcher.panel`.

- **Pre-create at launch, ordered out** — lazy creation pays first-`NSHostingView` render cost at the
  250 ms reveal.
- **`isOpaque = false` is load-bearing and gets a test.** `NSWindow.occlusionState` counts only
  *opaque* coverage, so a clear panel never flips it and `GhosttySurfaceView`'s occlusion path
  (`:441`, `:384`) never fires. Give the panel an opaque background later and terminal rendering
  stops behind it.
- ⌘` ignores it twice: `WindowRegistry.isCycleableWindow` (`:151`) requires `canBecomeKey`, plus
  `.ignoresCycle`. Drop `private` from that method so a test can assert it.
- Mouse works because `.onHover` uses `.activeInActiveApp` tracking areas and the app *is* active
  mid-shortcut; `acceptsFirstMouse` only matters when the app is inactive.
- Never `addChildWindow` it — `SCStreamConfiguration.includeChildWindows` defaults true and the panel
  would contaminate captures.
- Placement: centred in the key window's screen `visibleFrame`, recomputed per open.
- Panel touches no `AppStore`; the controller feeds value-type `SwitcherCard`s into
  `SwitcherRailModel` (`items`, `cursor`, `themeVersion`, `onHover`, `onCommit`).

**Invariant (prior learning `macapp-row-observes-sessions-invalidation-storm`):** no rail view may
hold an `AppStore` or `TerminalSessions`. `TerminalSessions` republishes per title/activity pulse; a
card observing it to compute "is cursor" would re-run at OSC frequency — the WORKROOM-2B hang.

### Rail

`Views/SwitcherRailView.swift` — horizontal `ScrollView` + `ScrollViewReader`, `HStack(spacing: 12)`,
`.sidebarCard(cornerRadius: 16, margin: 0, elevated: true)`, revealed with
`DialogOverlayStyle.revealAnimation`, `.scrollTo(cursor, anchor: .center)`, and a
`@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` snap path.

Card ≈ **220×140** (≈440×280 real px) — at 160×90 a downscaled terminal is illegible mush, which was
the outside voice's strongest argument against screenshots at all.
- thumbnail, or — when no snapshot exists — a **live text preview**: 2–3 tidied lines from
  `GhosttySurfaceView.readCommandRegion(maxBytes: 2_048)` (`:777`) + `TerminalCapture.tidy`, in the
  terminal font over `tokens.bg`. This is live even for hidden panes (occlusion stops rendering, not
  the terminal state machine) and needs no permission — it covers exactly what capture can't: a pane
  never visible this launch. Content panes fall back to their kind glyph (`plusminus` / `doc` /
  `clock`).
- title + subtitle from `AppStore.label(for:)`; `"Window \(windowNumber)"` as subtitle when one
  `SidebarID` appears in two windows.
- `UnreadBadge(count:)` top-trailing from `notifications.count(target:)` / `count(tab:)`.
- running dot from `TerminalTab.isRunning` / `terminals.isRunning(forTargetID:)`.
- cursor ring `strokeBorder(tokens.accent, lineWidth: 2)`; a11y ids `switcher.rail`,
  `switcher.card.<label>`.
- Text previews are synchronous main-thread libghostty reads: cursor ±3 only, lazily as the cursor
  moves, never from inside a libghostty callback.

### Capture

Own-process capture, verified in the SDK header (`SCShareableContent.h:151`):
`SCShareableContent.currentProcess` (macOS 14.4+) returns content "available to capture by current
process **without user consent via TCC**" — but the content is documented as *redacted*, so match on
`windowID` (`title`/`owningApplication` may be nil), and the no-TCC *capture* is still inference.
**Day-0 spike:** revoke Screen Recording for `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, capture our own
window, and assert a real `CGImage` **with non-uniform pixels** — not merely a non-nil filter.

One window capture per shot, N crops:

```swift
let scWindow = content.windows.first { $0.windowID == CGWindowID(nsWindow.windowNumber) }
let filter = SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow: scWindow)     // ignores overlapping windows
// size: s = min(1, 1440 / max(contentRect.width, contentRect.height) * pointPixelScale-adjusted)
config.width  = Int((filter.contentRect.width  * scale).rounded())
config.height = Int((filter.contentRect.height * scale).rounded())   // STRICTLY proportional
config.showsCursor = false
config.ignoreShadowsSingleWindow = true
config.ignoreGlobalClipSingleWindow = true
let image = try await SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: filter, configuration: config)
```

`pointPixelScale` and `contentRect` are **readonly on the filter** (`SCStream.h:114`, `:119`); the
config exposes only `width`/`height`/`scalesToFit` (`:212`, `:217`, `:239`). A long-edge cap with a
non-matching aspect letterboxes and silently misaligns every crop — so size proportionally, derive
**both** scaleX and scaleY from the delivered image, and assert they match.

Gate on `nsWindow.isVisible && !nsWindow.isMiniaturized && nsWindow.isOnActiveSpace` (a window on an
inactive Space can return an all-black *successful* image, which "keep the old entry on failure"
would not catch). Warm the SCK path once at idle — the first call initializes the subsystem for
hundreds of ms and would otherwise lose the 250 ms reveal race on the very first hold.

```
 request                                 resume
 ───────                                 ──────
 read epoch, window.frame,      ──▶ await capture ──▶  epoch changed? ──yes──▶ DISCARD whole shot
 and every visible region's                            frame changed? ──yes──▶ DISCARD
 screen rect (synchronously)                                  │no
                                                              ▼
                                              crop planned rects → downscale → cache
```

The epoch guard makes a mislabeled card structurally impossible; worst case is a stale one. Crop math
is pure and testable — both rects live in the same y-up screen space (`view.convert(bounds, to: nil)`
→ `window.convertToScreen`), so the global flip cancels: no `NSScreen` lookup, no multi-display case.


## Approved Plan:
# Issue #132 — Terminal/Workroom quick switcher (⌥Tab / ⌃Tab)

## Context

Workroom's navigation is entirely positional: ⌥⌘←/→ steps terminal tabs, ⇧⌥⌘←/→ steps workroom
tabs, ⌘1–9 / ⌥⌘1–9 jump by index, ⌘` cycles windows, ⌘[/] walks history. Nothing flips you back to
*what you were just looking at*, and nothing shows what's open without reading the tab bars.

Issue #132 asks for the macOS ⌘Tab experience, twice: **⌥Tab** for open workrooms across all app
windows, **⌃Tab** for the current workroom's detail panes. Quick tap switches immediately;
press-and-hold shows a screen-centred rail of screenshot thumbnails with labels and notification
badges; arrows/hover/click walk it; release commits.

Decisions taken with the user, then hardened through an engineering review + outside voice:
real screenshots (not text previews), MRU ordering, a floating panel so the rail can span windows,
all-windows scope, and **two shipped stages** — PR1 is tap-only and complete on its own, PR2 adds
hold-to-reveal and moves the commit to modifier release.

---

## Stage 1 (PR1) — tap-only MRU switching

No panel, no reducer, no release detection. Every ⌥Tab / ⌃Tab press commits immediately, exactly
like today's arrow cycling but ordered by recency. Ships as a complete sentence: "⌥Tab flips to the
workroom you were just in."

### Key routing

```
keyDown event
  │
  ├─ ⌘W branches (quick terminal, aux window)          ← unchanged, must stay first
  ├─ window = event.window ?? NSApp.keyWindow           ← unchanged
  ├─ ⌘` / ⇧⌘` window cycle                             ← unchanged
  │
  ├─ NEW: QuickSwitcherKey.classify(keyCode:flags:modifiers:) → .workrooms/.panes/nil
  │     │   keyCode 48 (Tab); modifiers come from Defaults (⌥ / ⌃ by default)
  │     ├─ event.isARepeat ................................ return nil  (swallow, don't spin)
  │     ├─ no store for `window` (quick terminal, Settings) return event (terminal keeps ⌃Tab)
  │     ├─ store.hasModalPresentation ..................... return nil  (swallow behind a sheet)
  │     ├─ switcher committed a switch .................... return nil
  │     └─ nothing to switch to (<2 items) ................ return event (⌃Tab reaches the TUI)
  │
  └─ existing ⌘1-9 / ⌥⌘1-9 / ⌘R / arrows / sidebar branches … → return event
```

Three things this deliberately does **not** do:
- **No `isAppShortcut` change and no `keyDown` hoist.** A static allowlist can't express "pass
  through when there's nothing to switch to", and the codebase already chose that side of the fork:
  ⌃⌘arrows is "deliberately **NOT** reserved — it passes through to the terminal at a split's edge"
  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989-990`). The monitor runs inside `NSApp.sendEvent` before dispatch, so
  when the switcher *does* act the surface never sees the key. Hoisting the classifier into `keyDown`
  would also have to land after the `onCloseRequested` "press any key to close" guard (`:834`) or it
  breaks run-pane closing — another reason not to touch that file.
- **No `flagsChanged` monitor** (nothing to detect in PR1).
- **No unconditional swallow.** Aux/quick-terminal windows and single-item cases return the event.

Gate on `store.hasModalPresentation` (`AppStore.swift:586`), **not** `activePicker`: the latter
misses `auxSheetPresented`, `pendingCommit`, `pendingDeletion`, `pendingProjectSettings`,
`pendingRemoteConfirm`, so ⌥Tab could otherwise retarget the selection under an open commit sheet.

### MRU

`Core/SwitcherRecency.swift`:

```swift
struct RecencyList<ID: Hashable> {                    // pure value type
  mutating func touch(_ id: ID); mutating func forget(_ id: ID); mutating func retain(_ live: Set<ID>)
  func ordered<T>(_ items: [T], id: (T) -> ID) -> [T] // MRU first, never-touched appended positionally
}
struct WindowToken: Hashable { let raw: UUID }         // AppStore.windowToken — NEVER reused
struct WorkroomSlotID: Hashable { let window: WindowToken; let sid: SidebarID }

@MainActor final class SwitcherRecency {
  static let shared = SwitcherRecency()
  func recordWorkroom(store: AppStore, sid: SidebarID?); func recordPane(_ id: TerminalTab.ID)
  func forgetPanes(_ ids: [TerminalTab.ID])
  func workroomOrder(_ slots: [WorkroomSlot]) -> [WorkroomSlot]
  func paneOrder(_ tabs: [TerminalTab]) -> [TerminalTab]
}
```

**Window identity is `let windowToken = UUID()` on `AppStore`** — not `windowNumber` (reclaimed by
`assignWindowNumberIfNeeded`, `WindowRegistry.swift:81-87`) and not `ObjectIdentifier(store)` (a
pointer; a new store at a freed address compares equal). `windowNumber` stays what it already is: the
`"Window \(n)"` display string (`AppStore.swift:1068`). This also means the snapshot cache needs no
purge-on-window-close hook to be *correct* — which matters, because `WindowRegistry.unregister`
(`:89`) has **no production caller** (only `RunCommandTests.swift:31` and `MultiWindowTests.swift:87`;
entries are reaped lazily by weak refs in `prune()`, `:94`).

Recording hooks — **all unconditional, above the `isNavigatingHistory` guard**:

| Hook | Site | Why unconditional |
|---|---|---|
| `recordWorkroom(store:sid:)` | `AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet` (`:157`) | `applyLocation` raises `isNavigatingHistory` for its whole body (`:3703`), and the switcher commits through it — a gated write would never fire |
| `recordWorkroom` | `WindowRegistry`'s existing `didBecomeKey` observer (`:48`) | without it, ⌘` to another window leaves MRU[0] on the window you left |
| `recordPane(tabID)` | `AppStore`'s `terminals.onFocusChange` (`:828`) | same suppression (`:836`); recency ≠ history |
| `forgetPanes(ids)` | `terminals.onTabsRemoved` (`:843`) | prune closed panes |

Panes key on `TerminalTab.ID` alone (a UUID, unique app-wide). Recency is in-memory/session-scoped.

### Item collection + commit

```swift
// workrooms: every window, MRU-ordered, frozen per press
WindowRegistry.shared.allStores
  .filter { !$0.hasModalPresentation }                  // can't switch into a busy window
  .flatMap { store in store.displayedWorkroomTargets().map { WorkroomSlot(store: store, …) } }
// panes: the key window's selected target only
store.terminals.tabs(for: target)
```

Commit, in this order (raise **first** — `persistsSidebarPrefs` keys on `lastActiveStore === self`,
`AppStore.swift:140`):

```swift
if !NSApp.isActive { NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true) }
store.hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)     // precedent: AppStore.swift:1972
store.openExisting(sid)                          // = NSApp.activate + applyLocation(target:tab:nil, recordHistory:true)
// panes:
store.terminals.select(tabID, for: target)       // `select`, not `focus` — fires onSurfaceFocused
```

**No new AppStore method.** `openExisting(_:)` (`:3775`) already *is* "select a workroom, restore its
focused tab, record one history entry". Skip the whole commit when the chosen identity is already
current: no raise, no write, no history entry (so ⌘[ isn't spammed).

### Shared wrap math

Extract `(current + step + count) % count` — written verbatim at `AppStore.swift:1156` and `:3444` —
into one pure `nonisolated static func wrapped(index:by:count:)`, reuse it in both cyclers and in the
switcher's MRU step. Existing coverage in `WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomsViewTests.swift` is the
regression net. (The outside voice called this make-work since the two cyclers differ in their
entry-when-absent behaviour; the user's call stands.)

### Label DRY

`fullTitle` is already duplicated at `WorkroomTabBar.swift:460` and `WorkroomSplitView.swift:437`;

## Stage 2 (PR2) — hold-to-reveal rail

Introduces the reducer, the panel, the rail and capture, and **changes commit timing from
press to modifier release** — an intentional behaviour change, called out in the PR body.

### Session state machine

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────── cancel(escape|deactivated|empty) ──────┐
                    │                                                                    ▼
   idle ──open(count>1)──▶ pending ──revealTimerFired(250ms)──▶ revealed ──modifierReleased──▶ idle
    ▲  │                     │  │                                 │  ▲                        │
    │  └─open(count<=1)──▶ idle  └──step──▶ revealed (immediate)   │  └─point/step (wrap ±)    │
    │                                                              └──commit(index) ───────────┘
    └──────────── every event while .idle is a no-op ◀── (click commit then modifier release)
```

`Core/QuickSwitcherReducer.swift`, in the shape of `EdgeRevealReducer`
(`Views/EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:30`):

```swift
enum Event { case open(kind:count:reverse:), step(reverse:), point(index:), revealTimerFired,
             commit(index: Int?), modifierReleased, cancel(Cancel), itemsChanged(count: Int) }
enum Effect { case none, armReveal, reveal, moveCursor(Int), end(commit: Int?) }
mutating func handle(_ event: Event) -> Effect
```

Load-bearing rules: `.idle` swallows everything (so a click commit followed by the inevitable
modifier release can't double-commit); `.step` while `.pending` reveals immediately (⌘Tab⌘Tab);
`revealTimerFired` outside `.pending` is a no-op (stale timer after a fast release);
`itemsChanged(0)` ends without commit, `>0` clamps. Reveal delay **250 ms**, one injected constant —
180 ms flashes on a chorded tap, and the "matches `EdgeRevealSidebar`" precedent was a misread (that
180 ms is a *hide* debounce at `:127`).

### Release detection — poll only

One 30 ms poll of `NSEvent.modifierFlags` while a session is live. It's a global hardware snapshot,
so it survives menu tracking, Mission Control and another app holding focus — the cases that starve a
local monitor, and Mission Control posts no `didResignActive` either. **No `flagsChanged` monitor**:
it would only buy latency, and it carries a real footgun (it must always `return event` or
`GhosttySurfaceView.flagsChanged`, `:927`, leaves libghostty believing ⌥ is still held).

Also live: `didResignActive` → cancel (you left the app, don't commit); `willClose` → re-resolve items
→ `itemsChanged`; Escape → cancel; a hard 10 s ceiling. Sticky Keys clears the ⌥ latch on the first
non-modifier key, so hold is unreachable for those users and the feature degrades to single-step flip
— documented, not worked around (no API detects it).

### Panel

`Core/SwitcherPanel.swift` — first `NSPanel` in the app. `QuickTerminalWindow` is **not** a
precedent (it's a plain `.titled NSWindow`, `QuickTerminalController.swift:7`, `:100`); only its
`.themeDidChange` observer (`:118`) is reusable.

```swift
final class SwitcherPanel: NSPanel {
  override var canBecomeKey: Bool { false }      // key stays with the workroom window → monitor keeps working
  override var canBecomeMain: Bool { false }
}
```

`[.nonactivatingPanel, .borderless]`, `isFloatingPanel = true`, `level = .floating`,
`collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .ignoresCycle, .transient]`,
`isOpaque = false`, `backgroundColor = .clear`, `hasShadow = false`, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`,
`isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true`, `animationBehavior = .none`, a11y id `switcher.panel`.

- **Pre-create at launch, ordered out** — lazy creation pays first-`NSHostingView` render cost at the
  250 ms reveal.
- **`isOpaque = false` is load-bearing and gets a test.** `NSWindow.occlusionState` counts only
  *opaque* coverage, so a clear panel never flips it and `GhosttySurfaceView`'s occlusion path
  (`:441`, `:384`) never fires. Give the panel an opaque background later and terminal rendering
  stops behind it.
- ⌘` ignores it twice: `WindowRegistry.isCycleableWindow` (`:151`) requires `canBecomeKey`, plus
  `.ignoresCycle`. Drop `private` from that method so a test can assert it.
- Mouse works because `.onHover` uses `.activeInActiveApp` tracking areas and the app *is* active
  mid-shortcut; `acceptsFirstMouse` only matters when the app is inactive.
- Never `addChildWindow` it — `SCStreamConfiguration.includeChildWindows` defaults true and the panel
  would contaminate captures.
- Placement: centred in the key window's screen `visibleFrame`, recomputed per open.
- Panel touches no `AppStore`; the controller feeds value-type `SwitcherCard`s into
  `SwitcherRailModel` (`items`, `cursor`, `themeVersion`, `onHover`, `onCommit`).

**Invariant (prior learning `macapp-row-observes-sessions-invalidation-storm`):** no rail view may
hold an `AppStore` or `TerminalSessions`. `TerminalSessions` republishes per title/activity pulse; a
card observing it to compute "is cursor" would re-run at OSC frequency — the WORKROOM-2B hang.

### Rail

`Views/SwitcherRailView.swift` — horizontal `ScrollView` + `ScrollViewReader`, `HStack(spacing: 12)`,
`.sidebarCard(cornerRadius: 16, margin: 0, elevated: true)`, revealed with
`DialogOverlayStyle.revealAnimation`, `.scrollTo(cursor, anchor: .center)`, and a
`@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` snap path.

Card ≈ **220×140** (≈440×280 real px) — at 160×90 a downscaled terminal is illegible mush, which was
the outside voice's strongest argument against screenshots at all.
- thumbnail, or — when no snapshot exists — a **live text preview**: 2–3 tidied lines from
  `GhosttySurfaceView.readCommandRegion(maxBytes: 2_048)` (`:777`) + `TerminalCapture.tidy`, in the
  terminal font over `tokens.bg`. This is live even for hidden panes (occlusion stops rendering, not
  the terminal state machine) and needs no permission — it covers exactly what capture can't: a pane
  never visible this launch. Content panes fall back to their kind glyph (`plusminus` / `doc` /
  `clock`).
- title + subtitle from `AppStore.label(for:)`; `"Window \(windowNumber)"` as subtitle when one
  `SidebarID` appears in two windows.
- `UnreadBadge(count:)` top-trailing from `notifications.count(target:)` / `count(tab:)`.
- running dot from `TerminalTab.isRunning` / `terminals.isRunning(forTargetID:)`.
- cursor ring `strokeBorder(tokens.accent, lineWidth: 2)`; a11y ids `switcher.rail`,
  `switcher.card.<label>`.
- Text previews are synchronous main-thread libghostty reads: cursor ±3 only, lazily as the cursor
  moves, never from inside a libghostty callback.

### Capture

Own-process capture, verified in the SDK header (`SCShareableContent.h:151`):
`SCShareableContent.currentProcess` (macOS 14.4+) returns content "available to capture by current
process **without user consent via TCC**" — but the content is documented as *redacted*, so match on
`windowID` (`title`/`owningApplication` may be nil), and the no-TCC *capture* is still inference.
**Day-0 spike:** revoke Screen Recording for `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, capture our own
window, and assert a real `CGImage` **with non-uniform pixels** — not merely a non-nil filter.

One window capture per shot, N crops:

```swift
let scWindow = content.windows.first { $0.windowID == CGWindowID(nsWindow.windowNumber) }
let filter = SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow: scWindow)     // ignores overlapping windows
// size: s = min(1, 1440 / max(contentRect.width, contentRect.height) * pointPixelScale-adjusted)
config.width  = Int((filter.contentRect.width  * scale).rounded())
config.height = Int((filter.contentRect.height * scale).rounded())   // STRICTLY proportional
config.showsCursor = false
config.ignoreShadowsSingleWindow = true
config.ignoreGlobalClipSingleWindow = true
let image = try await SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: filter, configuration: config)
```

`pointPixelScale` and `contentRect` are **readonly on the filter** (`SCStream.h:114`, `:119`); the
config exposes only `width`/`height`/`scalesToFit` (`:212`, `:217`, `:239`). A long-edge cap with a
non-matching aspect letterboxes and silently misaligns every crop — so size proportionally, derive
**both** scaleX and scaleY from the delivered image, and assert they match.

Gate on `nsWindow.isVisible && !nsWindow.isMiniaturized && nsWindow.isOnActiveSpace` (a window on an
inactive Space can return an all-black *successful* image, which "keep the old entry on failure"
would not catch). Warm the SCK path once at idle — the first call initializes the subsystem for
hundreds of ms and would otherwise lose the 250 ms reveal race on the very first hold.

```
 request                                 resume
 ───────                                 ──────
 read epoch, window.frame,      ──▶ await capture ──▶  epoch changed? ──yes──▶ DISCARD whole shot
 and every visible region's                            frame changed? ──yes──▶ DISCARD
 screen rect (synchronously)                                  │no
                                                              ▼
                                              crop planned rects → downscale → cache
```

The epoch guard makes a mislabeled card structurally impossible; worst case is a stale one. Crop math
is pure and testable — both rects live in the same y-up screen space (`view.convert(bounds, to: nil)`
→ `window.convertToScreen`), so the global flip cancels: no `NSScreen` lookup, no multi-display case.

```swift
enum SnapshotKey: Hashable { case pane(TerminalTab.ID), workroom(SidebarID, WindowToken) }
enum SnapshotGeometry {
  static func cropRect(regionOnScreen: CGRect, windowOnScreen: CGRect, imagePixelSize: CGSize) -> CGRect?
  static func thumbnailPixelSize(source: CGSize, maxPointWidth: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat) -> CGSize
}
```

Triggers — switcher-open (immediate, unbounded, fired **before** the panel is ordered in);
became-visible; activity-settled, gated on app-active **and** the window's `occlusionState`
containing `.visible`, at most once per ~3 s per window, never while a session is live; and
**theme change** (also bumps `themeGeneration`, so older entries read stale). No resize trigger — a
resize bumps the epoch, so no stale in-flight crop lands and the next natural capture fixes the card.
Honest limit: libghostty exposes no damage signal, so a shell producing output with no OSC won't
refresh between triggers; the escalation is a fork-side damage callback, not a tighter timer.

Cache: LRU, `maxEntries = 32`, byte cap, injected clock. Purge on `onTabsRemoved` and workroom
deletion. Rects come from a zero-drawing `SnapshotRectReporter` (`Views/`) registered in
`SnapshotRegistry`, mounted `.background { }` at exactly two always-mounted sites: `PaneLeafView`
(`Views/PaneTreeView.swift:383`, covers all four `TabContent` kinds) and `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:164`, covers solo *and* split since `RootView.workroomSplitBody`
always renders through `WorkroomSplitView`).

If the spike shows TCC *is* required: `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` for status (never prompt at
launch), `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` only from an explicit in-rail affordance, deep-link to
`x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture`, re-preflight on
`didBecomeActive`, and `Defaults[.railPreviews]` to opt out. Screen Recording needs no entitlement and
no Info.plist key; keep `CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS: NO` (`project.yml:299`). Add
`- sdk: ScreenCaptureKit.framework` to `project.yml`.

3	/// One visited location in the back/forward history (issue #26): a terminal target plus the
4	/// specific terminal tab focused there. `(target, tab)` is the whole identity — every focused
5	/// terminal is a distinct step (including the two on-screen panes of a split, and the neighbour
6	/// auto-focused after a close), so there is no split special-casing.
7	struct NavLocation: Equatable {
8	  let target: SidebarID
9	  /// The tab focused at the time. Always a real tab: a location is only ever recorded once a
10	  /// terminal is actually focused (see `AppStore.recordCurrentLocation`/`applyLocation`).
11	  let tab: TerminalTab.ID
12	  /// For a changeset tab, the commit it showed at record time — so the preview tab (retargeted across
13	  /// commits, which drifts its content) restores the right commit on replay. `nil` for other tabs.
14	  var commitID: String? = nil
15	  /// The commit's title, captured so replay can reopen the changeset without re-resolving it. `nil`
16	  /// unless `commitID` is set.
17	  var commitTitle: String? = nil
18	  /// The selected file at record time: the changed file within a changeset (or a diff tab's path).
19	  /// `nil` ⇒ the default (first) file. Makes each in-commit file selection its own step.
20	  var filePath: String? = nil
21	}
22	
23	/// A linear, browser-style back/forward history of visited terminal locations (issue #26).
24	///
25	/// ```
26	///   entries:  [ L0   L1   L2   L3 ]
27	///   cursor:           └ 1                back → L0 · forward → L2
28	///   record(L4) while cursor == 1  →  [ L0  L1  L4 ]   (forward truncated, L4 appended, cursor = 2)
29	/// ```
30	///
31	/// Pure value type (no SwiftUI/AppKit) so it is directly unit-testable, mirroring `RootPresentation`
32	/// / `AppStore.validatedSelection`. Liveness — is a recorded target/tab still alive? — is supplied by
33	/// the caller as an `isLive` predicate at `step` time; the history itself never resolves against
34	/// `AppStore`, so dead entries (a closed tab / deleted workroom) are skipped on replay rather than
35	/// pruned eagerly.
36	struct NavigationHistory {
37	  private(set) var entries: [NavLocation] = []
38	  /// Index of the current location in `entries`; `-1` when empty.
39	  private(set) var cursor: Int = -1
40	
41	  /// Upper bound on retained entries. When exceeded, the oldest fall off the front (and the cursor
42	  /// shifts with them) so a long session can't grow history without bound. Generous — a runaway
43	  /// backstop, not a tuning knob.
44	  static let maxEntries = 100
45	
46	  /// Whether there is an entry behind the cursor. Cursor-based (D2): liveness is only checked at
47	  /// `step` time, so this can be optimistically `true` even when every prior entry is dead.
48	  var canGoBack: Bool { cursor > 0 }
49	  /// Whether there is an entry ahead of the cursor (cursor-based — see `canGoBack`).
50	  var canGoForward: Bool { cursor >= 0 && cursor < entries.count - 1 }
51	
52	  /// The current location, or `nil` when empty.
53	  var current: NavLocation? { entries.indices.contains(cursor) ? entries[cursor] : nil }
54	
55	  /// Record a newly-visited location. No-op when it equals the current entry (dedup against the
56	  /// immediate cursor only — revisiting the same place in a row doesn't pile up). Otherwise any
57	  /// forward entries are truncated (you navigated somewhere new), the location is appended, and the
58	  /// total is capped at `maxEntries`.
59	  mutating func record(_ loc: NavLocation) {
60	    if current == loc { return }
61	    if cursor < entries.count - 1 {
62	      entries.removeSubrange((cursor + 1)...)
63	    }
64	    entries.append(loc)
65	    cursor = entries.count - 1
66	    if entries.count > Self.maxEntries {
67	      let overflow = entries.count - Self.maxEntries
68	      entries.removeFirst(overflow)
69	      cursor -= overflow
70	    }
71	  }
72	
73	  /// Drop every entry whose tab was removed (a closed tab / reaped workroom), so back/forward
74	  /// enablement stays honest — no entry that would no-op on replay survives (issue #26). The cursor
75	  /// is kept on the right surviving location: on the current entry if it survives, else just after
76	  /// the nearest surviving earlier entry (so Back lands on it). Any adjacent duplicate the removal
77	  /// exposes (the entry between two visits to the same place is gone) is collapsed, so Back never
78	  /// lands on a visibly identical location.
79	  mutating func prune(removing tabs: Set<TerminalTab.ID>) {
80	    guard !tabs.isEmpty, !entries.isEmpty else { return }
81	    let oldCursor = cursor
82	    var result: [NavLocation] = []
83	    var cursorIndex: Int? = nil  // new index of the surviving current entry, if it survives
84	    var survivorsBefore = 0  // count of (deduped) survivors with original index < oldCursor
85	    for (i, e) in entries.enumerated() {
86	      if tabs.contains(e.tab) { continue }
87	      let isDup = result.last == e
88	      if !isDup { result.append(e) }
89	      if i == oldCursor {
90	        cursorIndex = result.count - 1  // current survived (its slot, or the dup it merged into)
91	      } else if i < oldCursor, !isDup {
92	        survivorsBefore = result.count
93	      }
94	    }
95	    entries = result
96	    if result.isEmpty {
97	      cursor = -1
98	    } else if let cursorIndex {
99	      cursor = cursorIndex
100	    } else {
101	      cursor = min(survivorsBefore, result.count)  // current removed → after the last back-survivor
102	    }
103	  }
104	
105	  /// Move the cursor one step in `direction` (`-1` = back, `+1` = forward), skipping any entry the
106	  /// caller reports dead via `isLive`, and return the landed location. Returns `nil` — leaving the
107	  /// cursor unchanged — when there is no live entry that way. (With pruning this rarely skips; it's
108	  /// a defensive net.)
109	  mutating func step(_ direction: Int, isLive: (NavLocation) -> Bool) -> NavLocation? {
110	    var i = cursor + direction
111	    while entries.indices.contains(i) {
112	      if isLive(entries[i]) {
113	        cursor = i
114	        return entries[i]
115	      }
116	      i += direction
117	    }
118	    return nil
119	  }
120	}

10	///   context-menu actions act on whichever window is key (`keyStore`).
11	/// - **Last-active capture** — `lastActiveStore` tracks the most recent *workroom* window to become
12	///   key, captured before any modal (quit alert / Settings) can steal key status, so quit-time
13	///   persistence reads the right window.
14	/// - **Aggregation** — the Dock badge (and menu-bar item) sum across every window's notifications.
15	/// - **Run-command ownership** — a workroom's run command is single-owner across windows; a second
16	///   window's Run focuses the owner instead of forking a duplicate server (issue #70 / issue #7).
17	/// - **Quit/close de-dup** — `isTerminating` suppresses the per-window close prompt during a quit.
18	///
19	/// Per-window logic stays in `AppStore`; this holds only weak references, so closed windows fall out
20	/// on the next prune.

input.new_string:
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.
- **⌥Tab / ⌃Tab (the quick switchers, issue #132) are monitor-only and deliberately NOT in
  `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut`.** That list is static, but whether the app owns Tab depends on
  runtime state: a workroom with one pane has nothing to switch to, so ⌃Tab must reach the TUI. The
  monitor branch consumes the event only when a switch actually happened, exactly as ⌥⌘digit and
  ⌥⌘arrows already do — same reasoning as the unreserved ⌃⌘arrows. `AppShortcutReservationTests` pins
  Tab as never-reserved so a later "defence in depth" edit can't take `<C-Tab>` from every TUI. Both
  trigger modifiers are `Defaults` keys (`switcher*Modifier`) because a global-hotkey grabber
  (AltTab, HyperSwitch, Contexts all bind ⌥Tab) intercepts upstream of `NSApp.sendEvent`, where no
  local monitor can see the key and no API can detect the conflict.

**What ships**
