414	/// saturation and brightness; the monogram takes whichever of black/white is legible on the result.
415	private struct MarkWell: View {
416	  let mark: SwitcherMark
417	  /// Resolved by `SwitcherCard.cards(for:)`, once per reveal. `tileColor` is a search — a saturation
418	  /// ladder × brightness steps, each rung allocating an NSColor and measuring a contrast ratio — so
419	  /// running it from `body` re-ran it on every render of every card.
420	  let tile: NSColor?
421	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
422	
423	  var body: some View {
424	    let tile = tile ?? SwitcherMark.tileColor(hue: mark.hue, tokens: theme.tokens)
425	    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8, style: .continuous)
426	      .fill(Color(nsColor: tile))
427	      .frame(width: SwitcherRailLayout.wellSize.width, height: SwitcherRailLayout.wellSize.height)
428	      .overlay {
429	        Text(mark.monogram)
430	          .font(.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold, design: .rounded))
431	          .foregroundStyle(Color(nsColor: SwitcherMark.ink(on: tile)))
432	      }
433	  }
434	}
435	
436	/// A pane's type miniature, drawn from its own data.
437	private struct MiniatureWell: View {
438	  let miniature: PaneMiniature
439	  let palette: SwitcherRailLayout.Palette
440	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
441	
442	  var body: some View {
443	    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8, style: .continuous)
444	      .fill(theme.tokens.surface)
445	      .frame(width: SwitcherRailLayout.wellSize.width, height: SwitcherRailLayout.wellSize.height)
446	      .overlay { shape }
447	      .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8, style: .continuous))
448	  }
449	
450	  @ViewBuilder private var shape: some View {
451	    switch miniature {
452	    case .terminal(let running): terminal(running: running)
453	    case .diff(let change): diff(change)
454	    case .file: file
455	    case .changeset: changeset
456	    }
457	  }
458	
459	  /// A prompt chevron, with a filled pip while something is running — the one pane state you care about
460	  /// mid-switch is "is this the one that's still working".
461	  private func terminal(running: Bool) -> some View {
462	    HStack(spacing: 3) {
463	      Image(systemName: "chevron.right")
464	        .font(.system(size: 13, weight: .bold))
465	        .foregroundStyle(palette.name)
466	      if running {
467	        Circle().fill(palette.dot).frame(width: 5, height: 5)
468	      } else {
469	        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 1).fill(palette.subtitle).frame(width: 8, height: 2)
470	      }
471	    }
472	  }
473	
474	  /// Stacked add/remove bars. Composition follows the change *kind*, not magnitude: per-file line counts
475	  /// don't exist on `ChangedFile`, so an added file reads all-add, a deletion all-remove, a modification
476	  /// split, and a conflict takes the conflict token outright.
477	  private func diff(_ change: ChangedFile.Change) -> some View {
478	    VStack(spacing: 2) {
479	      ForEach(Array(bars(for: change).enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, bar in
480	        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 1)
481	          .fill(bar.color)
482	          .frame(width: bar.width, height: 4)
483	      }
484	    }
485	  }
486	
487	  private func bars(for change: ChangedFile.Change) -> [(color: Color, width: CGFloat)] {
488	    let add = palette.diffAdd
489	    let remove = palette.diffRemove
490	    switch change {
491	    case .added, .untracked:
492	      return [(add, 26), (add, 20), (add, 14)]
493	    case .deleted:
494	      return [(remove, 26), (remove, 20), (remove, 14)]
495	    case .modified, .other:
496	      return [(add, 26), (remove, 18), (add, 12)]
497	    case .renamed:
498	      return [(palette.subtitle, 26), (add, 18), (remove, 12)]
499	    case .conflicted:
500	      return [(Color(nsColor: theme.tokens.nsFg), 24), (remove, 24), (add, 24)]
501	    }
502	  }
503	
504	  /// Abstract text lines — a page, with no pretence of showing the real content.
505	  private var file: some View {
506	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
507	      ForEach([24, 18, 22, 13], id: \.self) { width in
508	        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 1)
509	          .fill(palette.subtitle)
510	          .frame(width: CGFloat(width), height: 2.5)
511	      }
512	    }
513	  }
514	
515	  /// A chain of commit dots.
516	  private var changeset: some View {
517	    HStack(spacing: 0) {
518	      ForEach(0..<3, id: \.self) { index in
519	        Circle()
520	          .fill(index == 0 ? palette.name : palette.subtitle)
521	          .frame(width: 6, height: 6)
522	        if index < 2 {
523	          Rectangle().fill(palette.subtitle).frame(width: 6, height: 1.5)
524	        }
525	      }
526	    }
527	  }
528	}

1	import AppKit
2	import Defaults
3	
4	/// Hosts one `QuickSwitcherReducer` session and connects it to the world (issue #132, T10): it freezes
5	/// the item list at open, arms the reveal, polls the trigger modifier, watches for the ways a session
6	/// can die, and performs the commit. The reducer decides; this only executes.
7	///
8	/// The panel is deliberately **not** owned here. `onReveal` / `onCursorMoved` / `onEnd` are the seam
9	/// T11 hangs the rail on, which keeps this whole class testable with no window on screen.
10	@MainActor
11	final class QuickSwitcherController {
12	  static let shared = QuickSwitcherController()
13	
14	  /// One frozen candidate. Frozen at open so the list can't reshuffle under the cursor mid-gesture —
15	  /// MRU order changes the instant anything is selected, which is exactly what a commit does.
16	  enum Item {
17	    case workroom(WorkroomSlot)
18	    case pane(TerminalTab)
19	  }
20	
21	  // MARK: Injected seams (production defaults; tests replace)
22	
23	  /// The live hardware modifier snapshot. A *global* read on purpose: it stays true through menu
24	  /// tracking, Mission Control and another app holding focus, all of which starve a local
25	  /// `flagsChanged` monitor. Masked to the device-independent bits — the raw value carries
26	  /// left/right-key and numeric-pad bits that never match a configured trigger.
27	  var flagsProvider: () -> NSEvent.ModifierFlags = {
28	    NSEvent.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
29	  }
30	
31	  /// D16: with VoiceOver running the switcher never opens a session — see `handleTrigger`.
32	  var voiceOverEnabled: () -> Bool = { NSWorkspace.shared.isVoiceOverEnabled }
33	
34	  /// Where the pointer is. Read at reveal *and* at each hover so D17's threshold compares two values
35	  /// from the same source — a test that injected only the hover position would be measuring against
36	  /// the real mouse, wherever the machine's cursor happens to sit.
37	  var pointerProvider: () -> NSPoint = { NSEvent.mouseLocation }
38	
39	  /// Speaks a destination on the VoiceOver path. Replaced in tests to assert what was announced.
40	  var announce: (String) -> Void = { message in
41	    NSAccessibility.post(
42	      element: NSApp as Any, notification: .announcementRequested,
43	      userInfo: [
44	        .announcement: message,
45	        .priority: NSAccessibilityPriorityLevel.high.rawValue,
46	      ])
47	  }
48	
49	  /// Starts the two production timers. Injected so tests can drive `revealTimerFired` / `poll`
50	  /// directly instead of waiting out real time.
51	  var startTimers: (QuickSwitcherController) -> Void = { controller in
52	    controller.installRealTimers()
53	  }
54	  var stopTimers: () -> Void = {}
55	
56	  // MARK: Rail seam (T11)
57	
58	  var onReveal: (([Item], Int) -> Void)?
59	  /// The item list changed mid-session and the rail must be re-rendered from it. Separate from
60	  /// `onCursorMoved`, which moves the highlight only: the rail is handed a frozen array at reveal, so
61	  /// without this the cards on screen and the array a commit indexes into drift apart.
62	  var onItemsChanged: (([Item], Int) -> Void)?
63	  var onCursorMoved: ((Int) -> Void)?
64	  var onEnd: (() -> Void)?
65	
66	  // MARK: State
67	
68	  private(set) var reducer = QuickSwitcherReducer()
69	  private(set) var items: [Item] = []
70	  /// The window the gesture started in — the commit's "am I already here" reference.
71	  private weak var originStore: AppStore?
72	  /// For a `.panes` session, the workroom whose panes are on the rail, frozen at open. Resolving it
73	  /// live off `originStore.selectedTarget` instead let a sidebar click (or a project reload) mid-gesture
74	  /// either kill every item or, worse, commit a pane into whatever workroom is selected *now*.
75	  private var paneTargetID: SidebarID?
76	  /// The modifier that must stay held. Released ⇒ commit.
77	  private var triggerFlags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = []
78	  private var observers: [NSObjectProtocol] = []
79	  private var pollTimer: Timer?
80	  private var revealTimer: Timer?
81	  private var ceilingTimer: Timer?
82	  /// Pointer position at reveal, for D17's movement threshold.
83	  private var pointerAtReveal: NSPoint?
84	
85	  var isLive: Bool { reducer.isLive }
86	  var isRevealed: Bool { reducer.isRevealed }
87	
88	  /// How far the pointer must actually travel before hover may steer the cursor (D17).
89	  static let hoverArmDistance: CGFloat = 4
90	
91	  /// How often the trigger modifier is sampled. Named alongside the reducer's `revealDelay` and
92	  /// `sessionCeiling` rather than left inline: it is the gesture's release latency, so it belongs with
93	  /// the other two numbers that define how the hold feels.
94	  static let pollInterval: TimeInterval = 0.03
95	
96	  // MARK: Entry
97	
98	  /// The key monitor's entry point. Returns whether the event was consumed.
99	  @discardableResult
100	  func handleTrigger(
101	    _ kind: QuickSwitcherKind, reverse: Bool, in store: AppStore,
102	    registry: WindowRegistry = .shared, recency: SwitcherRecency = .shared
103	  ) -> Bool {
104	    // D16 — VoiceOver: no session, no panel. ⌃⌥ is VoiceOver's own modifier pair, a panel that can't
105	    // become key can never hold VoiceOver focus however well it narrates, and a fast Tab-Tab-Tab would
106	    // queue announcements that land *after* the commit. So this degrades to the stage-1 tap flip, which
107	    // is a complete interaction on its own, and says where it landed.
108	    if voiceOverEnabled() {
109	      // VoiceOver can come on *mid-session* (or the rail can already be up when it does). Without this
110	      // the live session keeps its timers and its rail, the tap below commits immediately, and the
111	      // modifier release then commits a SECOND time off the frozen list.
112	      if isLive { cancel(.escape) }
113	      let outcome = QuickSwitcher.stepDescribing(
114	        kind, reverse: reverse, in: store, registry: registry, recency: recency)
115	      // Spoken from what the commit actually wrote, not from the origin store: a cross-window switch
116	      // leaves the origin's own selection untouched, so reading it back announced the workroom the user
117	      // just left — on the one path where the announcement *is* the entire UI.
118	      if let spoken = outcome.spoken { announce(spoken) }
119	      return outcome.switched
120	    }
121	
122	    if isLive {
123	      // A live session owns only its own kind and its own window. Dropping both (as this did) meant a
124	      // ⌃Tab landing inside the 30 ms poll window after ⌥ came up would step the *workroom* rail, eat
125	      // the key so the pane switch never happened, and then commit a workroom nobody asked for. Start
126	      // over instead: cancel and re-open for what was actually pressed.
127	      if kind == reducer.kind, store === originStore {
128	        apply(reducer.handle(.step(reverse: reverse)))
129	        return true
130	      }
131	      cancel(.escape)
132	    }
133	
134	    let frozen = Self.collect(kind, in: store, registry: registry, recency: recency)
135	    let effect = reducer.handle(.open(kind: kind, count: frozen.count, reverse: reverse))
136	    // Under 2 items there is nothing to switch to, so the key passes through to the terminal.
137	    guard effect != .none else { return false }
138	    items = frozen
139	    originStore = store
140	    paneTargetID = kind == .panes ? store.selectedTargetID : nil
141	    triggerFlags =
142	      (kind == .workrooms
143	      ? Defaults[.switcherWorkroomModifier] : Defaults[.switcherPaneModifier]).flags
144	    installObservers()
145	    startTimers(self)
146	    apply(effect)
147	    // A held modifier is not drivable by synthetic input (see `switcherRevealsImmediately`), so under
148	    // the fixture flag skip straight to the revealed state.
149	    if UITestFixture.switcherRevealsImmediately { revealTimerFired() }
150	    return true
151	  }
152	
153	  /// Escape while a session is live.
154	  @discardableResult
155	  func handleEscape() -> Bool {
156	    guard isLive else { return false }
157	    cancel(.escape)
158	    return true
159	  }
160	
161	  /// ←/→ while the rail is **up**, carrying nothing but the trigger modifier. Returns whether it was
162	  /// consumed.
163	  ///
164	  /// Both guards are load-bearing, and the branch that calls this used to have neither. `isRevealed`
165	  /// rather than `isLive`: during the 250 ms pending phase there is nothing on screen to steer, so
166	  /// eating an arrow there both swallowed the keystroke and popped the rail. And extra modifiers must
167	  /// disqualify it, or a live session steals ⌥⌘←/→ (terminal tabs), ⇧⌥⌘←/→ (workroom tabs) and
168	  /// ⌃⌘arrows (pane focus) — every one of which the user is already holding the trigger for.
169	  @discardableResult
170	  func handleArrow(reverse: Bool, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = []) -> Bool {
171	    guard isRevealed, flags.subtracting(triggerFlags).isEmpty else { return false }
172	    apply(reducer.handle(.step(reverse: reverse)))
173	    return true
174	  }
175	
176	  /// A card was hovered. Ignored until the pointer has actually moved (D17) — the reducer holds that
177	  /// rule; this only reports the movement.
178	  func point(index: Int, pointer: NSPoint? = nil) {
179	    guard isLive else { return }
180	    let location = pointer ?? pointerProvider()
181	    if let origin = pointerAtReveal,
182	      hypot(location.x - origin.x, location.y - origin.y) > Self.hoverArmDistance
183	    {
184	      pointerAtReveal = nil
185	      apply(reducer.handle(.armHover))
186	    }
187	    apply(reducer.handle(.point(index: index)))
188	  }
189	
190	  /// A card was clicked. Commits immediately; the modifier release that follows is swallowed.
191	  func clickCommit(index: Int) {
192	    guard isLive else { return }
193	    apply(reducer.handle(.commit(index: index)))
194	  }
195	
196	  func cancel(_ reason: QuickSwitcherReducer.Cancel) {
197	    guard isLive else { return }
198	    apply(reducer.handle(.cancel(reason)))
199	  }
200	
201	  // MARK: Timer / poll inputs (called by the real timers, or directly by tests)
202	
203	  func revealTimerFired() {
204	    apply(reducer.handle(.revealTimerFired))
205	  }
206	
207	  /// One 30 ms tick. The only thing that ends a held session normally.
208	  func poll() {
209	    guard isLive else { return }
210	    // Under the reveal fixture flag the "hold" is a synthetic tap, so the modifier is already up by
211	    // the time the first tick lands and the rail would vanish before anything could look at it. The
212	    // session then ends on Escape or a click, which is what those tests drive.
213	    guard !UITestFixture.switcherRevealsImmediately else { return }
214	    guard !flagsProvider().contains(triggerFlags) else { return }
215	    apply(reducer.handle(.modifierReleased))
216	  }
217	
218	  /// A window closed, a pane died, or a sheet went up: drop dead candidates, keep the cursor on the
219	  /// **item** it was tracking, and re-render the rail from the surviving list.
220	  ///
221	  /// Every part of that matters. `filter` compacts the array, so removing anything before the cursor
222	  /// shifts every later item down one — remapping by identity is what stops the release committing the
223	  /// card's neighbour. And the rail was handed a frozen array at reveal, so it has to be re-pushed or
224	  /// the cards on screen no longer line up with the array a click indexes into (a visible card then
225	  /// either switches to the wrong place or silently does nothing).
226	  func reconcileItems() {
227	    guard isLive else { return }
228	    let tracked = items.indices.contains(reducer.cursor) ? items[reducer.cursor] : nil
229	    let survivors = items.filter(isAlive)
230	    guard survivors.count != items.count else { return }  // nothing died; leave the rail alone
231	    items = survivors
232	    let remapped = tracked.flatMap { item in items.firstIndex { Self.sameItem($0, item) } }
233	    apply(reducer.handle(.itemsChanged(count: items.count, cursor: remapped ?? reducer.cursor)))
234	    if reducer.isRevealed { onItemsChanged?(items, reducer.cursor) }
235	  }
236	
237	  /// Identity, not index — the two things `reconcileItems` has to line up.
238	  private static func sameItem(_ lhs: Item, _ rhs: Item) -> Bool {
239	    switch (lhs, rhs) {
240	    case (.workroom(let a), .workroom(let b)): a.id == b.id && a.id != nil
241	    case (.pane(let a), .pane(let b)): a.id == b.id
242	    default: false
243	    }
244	  }
245	
246	  // MARK: Effects
247	
248	  private func apply(_ effect: QuickSwitcherReducer.Effect) {
249	    switch effect {
250	    case .none:
251	      break
252	    case .armReveal:
253	      break  // the timers were installed by `handleTrigger`; nothing to show yet
254	    case .reveal:
255	      // Record where the pointer already is, so a panel appearing under a stationary cursor can't
256	      // steer the selection (D17).
257	      pointerAtReveal = pointerProvider()
258	      onReveal?(items, reducer.cursor)
259	    case .moveCursor(let index):
260	      if reducer.isRevealed { onCursorMoved?(index) }
261	    case .end(let commit):
262	      let chosen = commit.flatMap { items.indices.contains($0) ? items[$0] : nil }
263	      let store = originStore
264	      let target = store.flatMap(frozenPaneTarget(in:))
265	      teardown()
266	      onEnd?()
267	      // `target` was read before `teardown()` cleared it.
268	      if let chosen, let store { Self.perform(chosen, from: store, target: target) }
269	    }
270	  }
271	
272	  private func teardown() {
273	    items = []
274	    originStore = nil
275	    paneTargetID = nil
276	    triggerFlags = []
277	    pointerAtReveal = nil
278	    for observer in observers { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(observer) }
279	    observers = []
280	    for timer in [pollTimer, revealTimer, ceilingTimer] { timer?.invalidate() }
281	    pollTimer = nil
282	    revealTimer = nil
283	    ceilingTimer = nil
284	    stopTimers()
285	  }
286	
287	  // MARK: Observers
288	
289	  private func installObservers() {
290	    let center = NotificationCenter.default
291	    observers = [
292	      // Left the app entirely (⌘Tab away, clicked another app) — don't commit somewhere they can't see.
293	      center.addObserver(
294	        forName: NSApplication.didResignActiveNotification, object: nil, queue: .main
295	      ) { [weak self] _ in
296	        MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.cancel(.deactivated) }
297	      },
298	      center.addObserver(forName: NSWindow.willCloseNotification, object: nil, queue: .main) {
299	        [weak self] _ in
300	        // Deferred: the window is still in `allStores` *during* willClose, so a same-tick re-resolve
301	        // would keep counting the one that's going away.
302	        DispatchQueue.main.async { MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.reconcileItems() } }
303	      },
304	    ]
305	  }
306	
307	  /// The production timers. `.common` run-loop mode is load-bearing: the default mode does not run
308	  /// during menu tracking or a modal loop, so a `.default`-mode poll would stall exactly in the cases
309	  /// the hardware-snapshot approach exists to survive, and the rail would hang until the mode exited.
310	  fileprivate func installRealTimers() {
311	    let reveal = Timer(
312	      timeInterval: Self.seconds(QuickSwitcherReducer.revealDelay), repeats: false
313	    ) { [weak self] _ in
314	      MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.revealTimerFired() }
315	    }
316	    let poll = Timer(timeInterval: Self.pollInterval, repeats: true) { [weak self] _ in
317	      MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.poll() }
318	    }
319	    let ceiling = Timer(
320	      timeInterval: Self.seconds(QuickSwitcherReducer.sessionCeiling), repeats: false
321	    ) { [weak self] _ in
322	      MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.cancel(.timeout) }
323	    }
324	    for timer in [reveal, poll, ceiling] { RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common) }
325	    revealTimer = reveal
326	    pollTimer = poll
327	    ceilingTimer = ceiling
328	  }
329	
330	  private static func seconds(_ duration: Duration) -> TimeInterval {
331	    let parts = duration.components
332	    return TimeInterval(parts.seconds) + TimeInterval(parts.attoseconds) / 1e18
333	  }
334	
335	  // MARK: Items
336	
337	  static func collect(
338	    _ kind: QuickSwitcherKind, in store: AppStore, registry: WindowRegistry = .shared,
339	    recency: SwitcherRecency = .shared
340	  ) -> [Item] {
341	    switch kind {
342	    case .workrooms:
343	      return QuickSwitcher.workroomSlots(registry: registry, recency: recency).map(Item.workroom)
344	    case .panes:
345	      return QuickSwitcher.paneTabs(in: store, recency: recency).map(Item.pane)
346	    }
347	  }
348	
349	  /// Still switchable? A slot whose window has gone (or has raised a sheet since) is dead; a pane is
350	  /// checked against its origin window's live tab list. An instance method, not a static: a pane's
351	  /// liveness is only answerable against *this* session's origin store.
352	  private func isAlive(_ item: Item) -> Bool {
353	    switch item {
354	    case .workroom(let slot):
355	      guard let store = slot.store, !store.hasModalPresentation else { return false }
356	      return store.displayedWorkroomTargets().contains { $0.sid == slot.sid }
357	    case .pane(let tab):
358	      guard let store = originStore, let target = frozenPaneTarget(in: store) else { return false }
359	      return store.terminals.tabs(for: target).contains { $0.id == tab.id }
360	    }
361	  }
362	
363	  /// The `.panes` session's workroom, resolved from the id frozen at open.
364	  private func frozenPaneTarget(in store: AppStore) -> TerminalTarget? {
365	    guard let sid = paneTargetID, let target = store.target(for: sid), !target.isMissing else {
366	      return nil
367	    }
368	    return target
369	  }
370	
371	  /// `target` is the session's frozen workroom, needed only by a pane commit.
372	  private static func perform(_ item: Item, from store: AppStore, target: TerminalTarget?) {
373	    switch item {
374	    case .workroom(let slot): QuickSwitcher.commit(slot, from: store)
375	    case .pane(let tab):
376	      guard let target else { return }
377	      QuickSwitcher.commit(pane: tab.id, in: store, target: target)
378	    }
379	  }
380	}

1	import AppKit
2	import SwiftUI
3	
4	/// The rail's geometry and colour decisions, kept pure so the parts that are easy to get *silently*
5	/// wrong are unit-testable without a panel on screen (issue #132, T11 / design decisions D9, D14, D15).
6	///
7	/// Nothing here draws. `SwitcherRailView` reads these; `SwitcherPanel` reads `viewportWidth`.
8	enum SwitcherRailLayout {
9	
10	  // MARK: Card geometry (D9)
11	
12	  /// The comfortable card width, used while the whole rail fits.
13	  ///
14	  /// Cards are **stacked** — well above label, the way ⌘Tab and the Dock put an icon above its name —
15	  /// rather than well-beside-label. That change alone nearly halved the card: a side-by-side card has to
16	  /// pay for the well's width *and* a label column beside it, while a stacked one gives the full card
17	  /// width to the label. Roughly twice as many workrooms now fit before the row has to scroll.
18	  static let maxCardWidth: CGFloat = 120
19	  /// The floor. The label spans the whole card here, so ~96pt of 12pt text survives — comfortably more
20	  /// than the side-by-side layout had at 180pt, where a 52pt well and its gap came off the top first.
21	  static let minCardWidth: CGFloat = 104
22	  static let cardHeight: CGFloat = 104
23	  static let cardSpacing: CGFloat = 8
24	  /// Inset from the rail's own edge to the first card.
25	  static let railPadding: CGFloat = 12

61	  /// clears a contrast floor. That is right for text and wrong here: on a light theme it walked every
62	  /// insufficiently-contrasty hue to near-black, so every tile collapsed into identical charcoal and the
63	  /// mark stopped marking anything — observed live before this existed.
64	  ///
65	  /// So hue is treated as identity and never adjusted; only saturation and brightness move, until the
66	  /// tile clears its floor against this theme's panel.
67	  static func tileColor(hue index: Int, tokens: ThemeTokens) -> NSColor {
68	    // Anchored on the theme's accent hue and spaced evenly around the wheel from there, so the marks
69	    // belong to the theme without being limited to the six ANSI slots — and a greyscale accent still
70	    // yields twelve usable angles.
71	    let accent = tokens.nsAccent.usingColorSpace(.sRGB)
72	    let anchor = (accent?.saturationComponent ?? 0) > 0.15 ? (accent?.hueComponent ?? 0) : 0
73	    let hueAngle = (anchor + CGFloat(index % hueCount) / CGFloat(hueCount)).truncatingRemainder(
74	      dividingBy: 1)
75	    let dark = tokens.colorScheme == .dark
76	    func ratio(_ color: NSColor) -> CGFloat { ThemeTokens.contrastRatio(color, tokens.nsPanel) }
77	    // Search brightness first, then give saturation ground — hue is identity and never moves.
78	    //
79	    // Two things this gets right that a single fixed walk did not, both measured rather than reasoned:
80	    //
81	    // 1. **Both directions.** The preferred one comes from `colorScheme`, which is derived from the
82	    //    theme's *background*, while the tile is measured against its *panel*. On a theme where those sit
83	    //    on opposite sides of mid-grey, a one-way walk moved the tile TOWARD the panel and nothing ever
84	    //    cleared 3:1.
85	    // 2. **Saturation is a fallback axis.** A mid-tone card caps how much contrast a saturated colour can
86	    //    reach at all: against this app's grey card (luminance 0.186) the *best* a 0.62-saturated hue can
87	    //    do is 2.71:1 at full brightness, because a saturated colour can't get light enough. Desaturating
88	    //    buys the luminance that brightness alone cannot — a pale blue clears the floor where a vivid one
89	    //    can't — and it stays visibly a hue, which a walk toward the foreground (`legible`) would not.
90	    let ladder: [CGFloat] = dark ? [0.55, 0.46, 0.38, 0.34] : [0.62, 0.52, 0.42, 0.34]
91	    var best: NSColor?
92	    for saturation in ladder {
93	      func tile(_ brightness: CGFloat) -> NSColor {
94	        NSColor(hue: hueAngle, saturation: saturation, brightness: brightness, alpha: 1)
95	      }
96	      let start: CGFloat = dark ? 0.72 : 0.62
97	      let lighter = Array(stride(from: start, through: 0.98, by: 0.03)).map(tile)
98	      let darker = Array(stride(from: start, through: 0.10, by: -0.03)).map(tile)

100	      if let clears = ordered.first(where: { ratio($0) >= Self.tileContrastFloor }) {
101	        return clears
102	      }

107	      }

112	    return best ?? NSColor(hue: hueAngle, saturation: ladder[0], brightness: 0.62, alpha: 1)

content.text: Measured the root cause — and it's bigger than T15's floors. Let me get your call before I touch app-wide colour behaviour:

questions.question: `ThemeTokens.luminance` never linearizes sRGB, so `contrastRatio` isn't WCAG — it under-reports badly. Measured across the 56 bundled themes: the rail's name text reads under 4.5:1 for **43** themes by the current metric vs **4** by real WCAG, and 38 themes therefore drop Liquid Glass for the opaque fallback. How far should the fix go?

options.label: Fix the metric app-wide (Recommended)
options.description: Linearize `luminance` (real WCAG), keep the old non-linear formula as `perceivedBrightness` for light/dark theme detection so appearance classification is unchanged, and make `contrastingForeground` pick ink by measuring both candidates instead of its luminance-0.6 threshold (the same flaw behind the 1.77:1 monogram). Root-cause fix: every floor in the app then means what it says, `legible` stops over-correcting, glass stays on for ~52/56 themes. Blast radius: contrast-corrected colours shift app-wide — diff syntax colours, badge/accent ink, sidebar nudges — all toward the theme's own colours. Needs a full test-suite pass; some theme tests assert current ratios.

options.label: Correct metric, rail only
options.description: Add a WCAG-correct helper used solely by the switcher's floors and the mark; leave every other consumer on the legacy metric. Zero visual change outside the rail, and the rail's 4.5/3.0 floors become honest. Cost: two contrast functions coexist with near-identical names, and the rest of the app keeps a metric labelled WCAG that isn't — including `contrastingForeground`, whose threshold bug stays live for the sidebar and toolbar badges.

options.label: Recalibrate the rail's floors
options.description: Change no logic — just lower the rail's constants until real themes pass under the existing metric (text ~3.0, indicators ~2.0, opaque-fill floor ~2.5). Smallest diff, keeps glass on. Cost: the numbers stop meaning WCAG anything, so the floors can no longer be reasoned about or reviewed against the standard, and any theme that is genuinely illegible passes too.

T15 asked for the rail's contrast floors to be verified against real bundled
themes. They could not be met, and the reason was the metric itself.

`ThemeTokens.luminance` weighted **gamma-encoded** sRGB components instead of
linearizing them first, so `contrastRatio` — documented as WCAG — was not WCAG.
It under-reports every dark colour (`#2E3440` reads 0.20 against a true 0.033),
which collapses dark-background/light-text ratios. Measured across the 56
bundled themes: the rail's 13pt name scored under 4.5:1 for **43** themes by
that formula and **4** by real WCAG, and `needsOpaqueFill` was firing for **38**
perfectly legible themes — two-thirds of the bundled set had quietly lost the
Liquid Glass surface.

So: `luminance` linearizes; the old formula stays as `perceivedBrightness` and
keeps `colorScheme` light/dark detection exactly as it was (WCAG luminance is
deliberately not perceptual — mid-grey linearizes to 0.216, which would classify
a visibly light background as dark); and `contrastingForeground` picks ink by
measuring both candidates rather than switching at luminance 0.6 — the same flaw
that left a monogram at 1.77:1 where black gave 11.8:1, so `SwitcherMark.ink`
collapses into a call to it.

The rail's badge pill is now the same corrected accent as the cursor ring, which
closes the judgment call flagged when the rail landed: `legible` walked the ring
away from a pale accent while the badge kept the raw one, so one card showed two
different "accents". `UnreadBadge` takes an optional fill/ink pair for that; its
default is unchanged everywhere else.

VoiceOver: a live session now ends (without committing) when VoiceOver comes on
mid-gesture. Via **KVO** on `NSWorkspace.isVoiceOverEnabled` — there is no
`voiceOverStatusDidChangeNotification` in AppKit, contrary to the plan; the
header says the property is "observable through KVO" and that is the only signal
there is. Per-cursor-move announcements are deliberately not added: D16 removed
the rail under VoiceOver, and with this watch there is no reachable state where a
cursor move happens with a screen reader listening.

New `SwitcherThemeSweepTests` asserts every role against every bundled theme
rather than two fixtures — text, indicators, all 12 tile hues and their
monograms, the badge on its own pill — plus the fallback/near-miss counts, so a
change that pushes half the set into the opaque fallback fails instead of passing
quietly. That sweep is what caught the metric.

1917/1917 unit tests pass; `make app-lint` clean; rail re-verified on screen.

name: contrast-metric-not-wcag
description: macapp's ThemeTokens.luminance was non-linearized (not WCAG) — fixed app-wide; perceivedBrightness keeps light/dark detection, contrastingForeground now measures both inks
metadata:

---

`ThemeTokens.luminance` weighted gamma-encoded sRGB instead of linearizing, so `contrastRatio`
(documented as WCAG) under-reported every dark colour — `#2E3440` read 0.20 vs a true 0.033. Effect
measured over the 56 bundled ghostty themes: the switcher rail's name text failed 4.5:1 for **43**
themes (4 by real WCAG) and `needsOpaqueFill` killed Liquid Glass for **38** legible themes.

Fixed 2026-08-05 (`dfcc0bd8`), app-wide, with Joel's explicit approval of the blast radius:
- `luminance` linearizes (real WCAG); every floor in the app now means what it says.
- The old formula survives as `perceivedBrightness`, used **only** by `colorScheme` light/dark
  detection — WCAG luminance is not perceptual (mid-grey = 0.216 linear), so a 0.5 threshold against
  it would classify visibly light backgrounds as dark.
- `contrastingForeground` picks black/white by **measuring both ratios**, no luminance-0.6 threshold
  (that threshold was the 1.77:1 monogram bug). `SwitcherMark.ink` is now just a call to it.

**How to check a contrast claim here:** sweep the bundled themes (`SwitcherThemeSweepTests` reads
`Bundle.main.resourceURL/ghostty/themes` directly, never `ThemeService.themeDirectories()` whose first
entry is the user's `~/.config`). Two hand-made fixtures prove nothing — see
[[ambient-theme-tests-hide-contrast-bugs]].

**Why it matters:** any new floor added against this metric before the fix was silently ~2× too
strict for dark themes.

[[defaults-launch-arg-string-shadow]]) or accept the claim can't be checked live and verify it by
measurement in a unit test. If a real domain does get touched, restore it immediately and say so.

**T14 and T15 done — the last two open tasks on the plan. Two commits.**

**T14 (`5fc3cdee`) — Go ▸ Last-Used Workroom / Last-Used Pane.** Key equivalents rendered from the `Defaults` chords, which is how macOS teaches a shortcut, plus the only mouse-reachable route into the feature.

`ThemeTokens.luminance` weighted **gamma-encoded** sRGB instead of linearizing it, so `contrastRatio` — documented as WCAG — wasn't. Across the 56 bundled themes the rail's name text scored under 4.5:1 for **43** themes by that formula and **4** by real WCAG, and `needsOpaqueFill` was firing for **38 legible themes** — two-thirds of the bundled set had quietly lost the Liquid Glass surface you asked for. VoiceOver coming on mid-gesture ends the session without committing — via **KVO**, because the notification the plan named doesn't exist; `isVoiceOverEnabled` is KVO-only. Per-cursor-move announcements are deliberately absent: D16 removed the rail under VoiceOver, so with that watch there's no reachable state where a cursor move happens with a screen reader listening.

  because a global-hotkey grabber (AltTab, HyperSwitch, Contexts all bind ⌥Tab) intercepts upstream of

  user is a preference they currently can't reach. The Keyboard Shortcuts sheet already renders the
  configured chords (`SwitcherModifier.display`), so the picker is the missing half.
- **Scope ⌥Tab to the current Space.** A cross-window commit to a window on another Space animates the

  instant. Either filter `QuickSwitcher.workroomSlots` by `hostWindow?.isOnActiveSpace` (and lose the
  ability to reach those workrooms at all) or leave it; decide from use, not from taste.

  (`Palette.nsBadgeFill` == `nsRing`, ink measured), because a themed accent can sit close to the
  surface it's on — the sidebar and toolbar badges have the same exposure and no correction. Now a
  small change: `ThemeTokens.contrastRatio` is genuinely WCAG since `dfcc0bd8`, so
  `legible(accent, on: host, target: 3.0)` at the component's own call sites means what it says.

### Harden `vcs.Detect` to validate a real repo (CLI) — #103 follow-up

**What:** `vcs.Detect` (`internal/vcs/vcs.go`) currently treats a directory as a repo if `.jj` is a
dir OR `.git` merely *exists* (file or dir). A bogus/empty `.git` therefore registers as a project
via `add-project` and only fails later, at workroom creation.

**Why:** Surfaced by the Codex outside-voice pass during `/plan-eng-review` of issue #103 (the
create-project work). It's a pre-existing robustness gap — the existing-path `add-project` already
has it; #103's create flow inits a real repo so its happy path is unaffected — but a stricter check
would fail fast with a clear error instead of a confusing late failure. Re-confirmed by the Codex
pass during the jj→git stale-vcs fix: the new reconcile-on-list (`Service.effectiveVCS`) also uses
marker-file truth, so a *present-but-broken* `.jj` dir would still reconcile as jj — hardening
`Detect` fixes both the late-failure gap and the reconcile accuracy in one place.

**How to start:** In `Detect`, validate beyond existence — e.g. `git rev-parse --git-dir` (or read
`.git`/`HEAD`) for git, and confirm `.jj/repo` for jj. Weigh that `Detect` runs on every
create/list/delete (now also list-reconcile), so keep it cheap (a stat-level check may suffice over
forking git).

**Depends on:** nothing; touches all VCS consumers (`create`, `list`, `delete`, `add-project`).

**2026-08-05 — the ⌥Tab / ⌃Tab quick switcher (#132), and the contrast metric it exposed.** ⌥Tab steps
open workrooms across every window by most-recent use, ⌃Tab steps the current workroom's panes; a tap
flips, a 250ms hold reveals a screen-centred rail of cards, release commits. `Core/SwitcherRecency.swift`
(pure `RecencyList` + `WindowToken`), `QuickSwitcher{,Reducer,Controller}.swift`, `SwitcherPanel.swift`,
`SwitcherRailLayout.swift`, `SwitcherMark.swift`, `Views/SwitcherRailView.swift`, plus Go-menu items and
two Keyboard Shortcuts rows. Deferrals are filed above ("Quick-switcher deferrals"). The traps:

- **`ThemeTokens.luminance` was never WCAG.** It weighted *gamma-encoded* sRGB instead of linearizing,
  so `contrastRatio` under-reported every dark colour (`#2E3440` read 0.20 against a true 0.033). Across
  the 56 bundled themes the rail's name text scored under 4.5:1 for **43** of them by that formula and
  **4** by real WCAG, and the "this theme is unreadable, drop the material" fallback was firing for 38
  legible themes. Fixed app-wide: `luminance` linearizes, the old formula survives as
  `perceivedBrightness` for light/dark classification only (WCAG luminance is not perceptual), and
  `contrastingForeground` picks ink by **measuring both candidates** instead of a luminance-0.6 switch —
  that threshold is what left a monogram at 1.77:1 where black gave 11.8:1.
- **Contrast tests must pin their theme, and then sweep the real ones.** Three "failures on untouched
  code" were tests reading the ambient theme via `ThemeTokens(preview: nil)`, which follows the machine's
  appearance. Pinning them to fixtures exposed two real bugs; sweeping all 56 bundled themes
  (`SwitcherThemeSweepTests`) exposed the metric. Two hand-made fixtures prove nothing about the
  fiftieth theme.
- **A borderless non-opaque `NSPanel` casts no shadow at all** (measured: zero darkening at 6/14/26/44pt
  out with `hasShadow = true` + `invalidateShadow()`). The rail draws its own — which needs the window
  padded by a halo (a drawn shadow clips at the window edge), the shadow in a *second* `.background`
  after `.clipShape` (a clip applies to a view's background), and the caster's own footprint punched out
  with `destinationOut`, because an opaque layer anywhere beneath a glass view annihilates the material
  (interior variation and backdrop correlation both fall to exactly 0).
- **Compacting a live item list silently retargets the commit.** `filter`ing dead items shifted every
  later index down one while the reducer only *clamped* the cursor, so losing an item before the cursor
  committed the highlighted card's neighbour — and the rail was never re-pushed, so a click indexed a
  stale array. `.itemsChanged` now carries a cursor remapped by item **identity**.
- **A commit must re-check `hasModalPresentation`.** It was enforced at open and in the liveness check,
  which only runs on a window *close* — a sheet going up posts no notification the session watches, so
  releasing over a window that had since become modal performed exactly the write the gate exists to
  prevent.
- **Raising a window fires the recency hook for the selection it's leaving**, so MRU[1] became somewhere
  the user had never been and the ⌥Tab⌥Tab ping-pong broke. `SwitcherRecency.suppressingRecord` wraps the
  raise.
- **There is no VoiceOver-status notification in AppKit.** `isVoiceOverEnabled` is KVO-only
  (`NSAccessibility.h`), which is how a live session now ends when VoiceOver arrives mid-gesture.
- **`UserDefaults` is not isolated by a throwaway `$HOME`** — cfprefsd resolves the login session's home,
  so QA can isolate `~/.config/workroom` but never `Defaults`-backed state (theme, inspector, channel).
  Use a `UITestFixture` flag instead.
- **Window captures were built (T12) and removed.** At card size an aspect-fit terminal thumbnail is a
  grey smudge that changes every time and looks like every other terminal — it carried the least
  information while being the loudest element. Replaced by a learnable per-workroom mark (hue + monogram,
  hues rotated so no two visible cards collide) and a per-pane type miniature. `Core/Snapshots/` is gone;
  own-process ScreenCaptureKit needing no TCC was proven on the way and is in git history if it's ever
  wanted again.

**2026-07-26 — the shared inspector prefs are out of the test suite, and the fix went one class further
than filed.**

content.text:
**No — `TODOS.md` had nothing about #132 at all.** Fixed and pushed (`b376ea47`).

The #132 plan's out-of-scope table said "add to `TODOS.md` at implementation time" for several items and that never happened. Now filed as one entry, six items:

- **MRU order in the ⌘O picker** — cheap once `SwitcherRecency` exists, but it reorders a shipped tested surface.
- **Settings picker for the two trigger modifiers** — the keys ship with no UI, so retuning needs `defaults write`. **P2 for anyone running AltTab/HyperSwitch/Contexts**: they bind ⌥Tab upstream of `NSApp.sendEvent`, so for those users the switcher never fires and the only remedy is a preference they can't reach.
- **Scoping ⌥Tab to the current Space** — a cross-Space commit animates for ~0.5–1s.
- **The shared `UnreadBadge` still draws the raw accent** — only the rail's badge got the corrected pair. Now a small change, since the metric fix made `legible(..., target: 3.0)` mean what it says.
- **The 10s ceiling cancels silently** — hold ⌥ for eleven seconds and you get nothing; arguably it should commit the cursor. Your call.
- **⌃-click on the pane rail is unverified** — secondary click on a never-key panel; needs a real mouse, since synthetic input has lied here twice.

Two plan TODOs are **moot**: window captures were built and removed, so "libghostty damage callback for thumbnail freshness" and "per-pane sensitive marking / screen-sharing suppress" have no subject — `Core/Snapshots/` is gone.

Also added a **Recently done** entry, since that section is where this repo keeps the traps: the non-WCAG luminance, why contrast tests must pin their theme *and* sweep the real 56, the panel-casts-no-shadow measurements, the index-vs-identity commit bug, the missing modal re-check, the phantom MRU record from a window raise, KVO being the only VoiceOver signal, and `$HOME` not isolating `UserDefaults`.
